item.content:encoded:
A week or two ago, Tuesday’s doubleheader loomed as perhaps the largest day (and night) of the Yankees season.
But the Rays separating themselves — entering with a six-game lead that had doubled since Sept. 11 — and requiring just one victory in this four-game set to clinch the division drained much of the drama from the opening game of the series at a half-filled Stadium.




Access the Yankees beat like never before


Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
And so a strong afternoon effort by the Yankees encouraged and kept their AL East hopes alive, but it more kept those hopes on a ventilator than revive them.
In the first of two games on the day, the Yankees beat the Rays 2-0 in front of an announced crowd of 41,421 in The Bronx during a brisk late-September afternoon that hinted at October.
In all likelihood, also coming soon is the Rays wrapping up the division, but the Yankees (90-66) at least did not allow their rival to celebrate on their grass immediately. Of course, the Rays (95-61) have three more chances to do so, including another that was set for just a few hours later.
“We all believe in each other in this locker room and not looking too far ahead,” said Cody Bellinger, who provided the only run-scoring swing in the victory that clinched no worse than the top wild-card spot.
The Yankees are nearly guaranteed a first-round home date with the Red Sox in a best-of-three series that likely would not include their best player: The club is operating under the belief Aaron Judge will not be available for the series because of his calf strain.
If Aaron Boone’s bunch is going to escape the Red Sox and face off with these same Rays in the ALDS, they would have to rely on their stars rather than their superstar.
On that front, Tuesday afternoon provided some hope with Carlos Rodón (eight shutout, overpowering innings in which he faced just one over the minimum) and Bellinger (a two-run blast in the fourth inning that provided the only runs the club needed) stepping up.
“Just a really solid, quick win,” Boone said of a game that lasted just 2 hours, 2 minutes in large part because of Rodón’s dominance and efficiency, which bodes well for the postseason even if Rodón probably would not get a first-round start.
In his longest, best and likely last outing of the regular season, Rodón struck out eight and allowed just three base runners on three singles.
The first two were erased by double plays (the second, in the sixth inning, entailed Bellinger catching a Richie Palacios line drive and throwing strong to first to double up Victor Mesa Jr.).
The third was a one-out single to Jonathan Aranda in the seventh inning, which might have presented the greatest threat to Rodón. But against Junior Caminero — an MVP candidate who represented the tying run — the veteran reached back for his two hardest pitches of the game (both 97.5 mph fastballs) to get ahead 0-2 before finishing Caminero off with a slider.
“He was awesome. Strike throwing was great,” Boone said of Rodón, who needed 96 pitches to record 24 outs, won his 100th career game and tallied his 1,500th strikeout. “… [He had] velo when he really needed it.”
The Yankees offense was held down by Nick Martinez for three perfect innings before pouncing on two consecutive imperfect pitches to begin the bottom of the fourth.
Ben Rice roped a double down the right field line for the first Yankees hit before Bellinger got a first-pitch sinker across the middle of the plate and clubbed it to right for his 17th homer of the season.
And that was all Rodón needed in a game that might have given the club a blueprint for how it can succeed in October against a team like the Rays and without a monstrous presence like Judge.
“You see the defense today — we’re solid,” said Rodón, who praised José Caballero (a bunt single and two steals in an empty fifth inning) before addressing the rest of the club. “Some lengthy at-bats. Some big-time hits — the homer from Beli there. The bullpen is deep.
“The starters are really good. I have a lot of confidence in this club.”

item.title: [morningjournal.com] Yankees star Aaron Judge has injection in sore right calf, unlikely to play in the Wild Card Series
item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: By Larry Fleisher The Associated Press NEW YORK — Yankees slugger Aaron Judge is unlikely to play in the Wild Card Series after having an injection in his sore right calf, manager Aaron Boone said Tuesday. Before the Yankees faced the Rays in a day-night doubleheader, Boone said Judge had a platelet poor plasma injection during the team’s off-day on Monday following its return from Arizona. “We’re planning on him not being a part of that (Wild Card Series) but we’re also at time of the year, you
item.content:encoded:
By Larry Fleisher
The Associated Press
NEW YORK — Yankees slugger Aaron Judge is unlikely to play in the Wild Card Series after having an injection in his sore right calf, manager Aaron Boone said Tuesday.
Before the Yankees faced the Rays in a day-night doubleheader, Boone said Judge had a platelet poor plasma injection during the team’s off-day on Monday following its return from Arizona.
“We’re planning on him not being a part of that (Wild Card Series) but we’re also at time of the year, you hear all the time with injuries, you give ranges two to four weeks, four to six weeks,” Boone said. “The range is for a reason and we’re at a point of the year where obviously we push it a little bit if that was in play but that’s a week away. I’m not expecting it, but I’m not ruling it out either.”
The Yankees will most likely play the Boston Red Sox in the first round of the postseason.
Judge was put on the 10-day injured list Saturday with a strained soleus muscle, which is in the lower part of his calf. Boone did not say what grade the strain is but described it as “moderate.”
Judge is eligible to be activated for the regular-season finale on Sunday against Baltimore but will not do much activity in the next few days.
Judge injured his calf during last Wednesday’s game at Minnesota. The eight-time All-Star was lifted in the sixth inning for a pinch hitter because of discomfort in his leg and said at the time it was a precautionary move.
Boone said symptoms persisted and an MRI revealed the strain.
Judge was 4 for 23 with 13 strikeouts and one extra-base hit in seven games after returning Sept. 8 from a broken rib, which kept him out of the lineup for more than three months.
Judge is hitting .241 with 18 homers and 41 RBIs in just 66 games this year. He hit a long homer on Sept. 14 in Minnesota and had the next game off before straining his calf.
The Yankees entered Tuesday with a 48-41 record in the games Judge has missed and a 41-25 mark in games he has played. New York also began Tuesday a loss away from being eliminated from the AL East race, setting up a second straight wild-card series against the Red Sox next week.
“We’ve played much of the year without him and for the most part, we’ve done a pretty good job,” Boone said. “So guys are used to it. Obviously you always want your best player in the mix, but we understand we’ve got a job to do and an expectation to win. I think that expectation doesn’t change with or without him. We’re expecting to go into the series and know we can beat anyone when we play our game.”

item.content:encoded:
Yankees de Nueva York jugarían la Ronda de Comodines de la MLB 2026 sin su capitán, Aaron Judge; esta es la razón
A la temporada regular de las Grandes Ligas aun le quedan 2 series para disputar por equipo, siendo el próximo martes 29 de septiembre cuando comiencen la Ronda de Comodines, en donde Yankees podría jugar sin Aaron Judge.
Los Yankees de Nueva York afrontarán posiblemente una eventual Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana ante los Medias Rojas de Boston sin su capitán, Aaron Judge.
El manager del equipo, Aaron Boone confirmó este martes 22 de septiembre que el equipo trabaja con el escenario de no contar con Judge, aunque dejó abierta la posibilidad de acelerar su recuperación si la situación lo requiere.
¿Por qué Aaron Judge no podría jugar la Ronda de Comodines con Yankees?
El beisbolista de estadounidense de 34 años sufrió una distensión de "grado moderado" en la pantorrilla derecha y tiene comprometida su presencia en el inicio de la postemporada.
Judge fue colocado el pasado sábado en la lista de lesionados de 10 días, con efecto retroactivo al 17 de septiembre, después de sufrir la distensión durante la serie de la semana pasada contra los Mellizos de Minnesota.
El toletero recibió el lunes una inyección de plasma pobre en plaquetas y tendrá actividad limitada durante los próximos días. "El par de días siguientes no habrá mucho: nada de correr, saltar, cosas así", indicó Boone.
Judge explicó que la lesión afecta al músculo sóleo de la pantorrilla derecha, una zona que considera especialmente importante para correr y batear.
"He lidiado con distensiones antes y de alguna manera he jugado con ellas, pero esta fue en un lugar diferente donde lo hizo un poco más difícil", comentó Judge.
¿Cuánto tardaría en recuperarse Aaron Judge para volver a jugar con Yankees?
Una distensión de grado 2 en la pantorrilla suele requerir entre 3 y 6 semanas de recuperación, un plazo que complica su presencia en el comienzo de los playoffs.
"Si él es capaz de jugar, entonces le daremos esa oportunidad", señaló Boone.
Judge, que ya se perdió buena parte del verano por una fractura en la costilla derecha, apenas disputó siete partidos desde su regreso en septiembre.
En 66 encuentros esta campaña bateó .241/.360/.511, con 18 jonrones y 41 carreras impulsadas
Los Yankees ya aseguraron su boleto a los playoffs, pero una victoria de los Rays de Tampa Bay en cualquiera de los encuentros de la doble cartelera de este martes 22 de septiembre les permitiría conquistar el Este de la Liga Americana y el primer sembrado de la liga, lo que enviaría a Nueva York a disputar la Serie del Comodín.
Yankees Manager Aaron Boone said today that the team is not planning on Aaron Judge being available for the Wild Card series. pic.twitter.com/1ecutsoJrt
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) September 22, 2026

item.title: [yardbarker.com] Carlos Rodon reaches multiple career milestones in victory over Rays
item.dc:creator: Bill Ladson
item.description: NEW YORK — It’s safe to say New York Yankees left-hander Carlos Rodón is ready for the postseason. He pitched his best game of the season in a 2-0 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium on Tuesday afternoon. Rodón pitched a season-high eight innings, allowed three hits and struck out eight batters. item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK — It’s safe to say New York Yankees left-hander Carlos Rodón is ready for the postseason. He pitched his best game of the season in a 2-0 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium on Tuesday afternoon.
Rodón pitched a season-high eight innings, allowed three hits and struck out eight batters. It was a quick game, which lasted two hours and two minutes.
“He was awesome,” Yankees manager Aaron Boone told reporters about Rodón. “His strike throwing was great. The fastball was in a really good place, a really good profile in the heater, too. The secondary (pitches) were good — the slider and changeup. … It was a really solid quick win.”
Rodón also reached a couple of milestones along the way, striking out his 1,500th batter in the seventh and winning his 100th game of his career. Rodón said when he started his big-league career with the Chicago White Sox on April 21, 2015 against the then-Cleveland Indians, he wasn’t looking into the future thinking that he was going to win a lot of games.
“At 22 (years old), it was a cold night in Chicago,” Rodón recalled to reporters. “I ran out to the mound and never saw three decks in a stadium before. So I was trying to keep my heart in my chest. The crystal ball wasn’t looking this far into the future.”
Rodón wasn’t nervous against the Rays, however. He had 18 swings and misses, and his fastball went as high as 97.5. For his 1,500th strikeout, Rodón struck out Jonny DeLuca on a 86.3 mph slider.
“During the moment, I didn’t know what was going on. I go, people are clapping. Cool. Fifteen hundred is nice. Hopefully, I can keep going,” Rodón said.
Rodón most likely started his last game of the season, although Boone hasn’t ruled out Rodón throwing on Sunday against the Orioles. The Yankees will go into the postseason without their best player, Aaron Judge. But Rodón is confident that the team will go far. He based it on what he saw in Tuesday’s game.
Cody Bellinger was clutch with a two-run homer in the fourth frame and was able to double off Victor Mesa Jr. at first base after Richie Palacio flew out to Bellinger in left field two-innings later.
“The bullpen is deep. The starters are really good. I have a lot of confidence in this club,” Rodón said.
All quotations obtained firsthand unless otherwise noted.

item.title: [fansided.com] Projecting the Yankees Wild Card series lineup after brutal Aaron Judge's injury update
item.dc:creator: Zachary Rotman
item.description: It felt like Aaron Judge was returning at the perfect time. A September return following a three-month stint on the IL gave Judge enough time to find his timing before the postseason. Unfortunately, Judge suffered another injury before the playoffs even began, hurting his calf in a game against the Minnesota Twins. The New York Yankees hoped it'd be minor, but it was serious enough for the team to place its captain on the Injured List. Now, it sounds as if a return for the Yankees' first postsea
item.content:encoded:
It felt like Aaron Judge was returning at the perfect time. A September return following a three-month stint on the IL gave Judge enough time to find his timing before the postseason. Unfortunately, Judge suffered another injury before the playoffs even began, hurting his calf in a game against the Minnesota Twins. The New York Yankees hoped it'd be minor, but it was serious enough for the team to place its captain on the Injured List. Now, it sounds as if a return for the Yankees' first postseason series is a long shot at best.
A "moderate grade" calf strain is serious enough for Yankees manager Aaron Boone to proceed as if his best player won't be active at all for the Wild Card series. That is an insanely difficult blow for a Yankees team that, with Judge, is as good as any in a weak American League. For the Yankees to advance to the ALDS and potentially get their captain back, they'll need to rely on this projected lineup below.
What the Yankees lineup could look like without Aaron Judge
Judge is an instrumental piece in the Yankees' lineup for a couple of reasons. First, he's the best hitter in the sport when healthy. That obviously matters. Second, Judge is one of the few right-handed bats on this roster. He provides much-needed balance that, without Judge, the Yankees lack.
| Position | Player |
|---|---|
| Ben Rice | DH |
| Cody Bellinger | LF |
| Heliot Ramos | RF |
| Luis Garcia Jr. | 1B |
| Spencer Jones | CF |
| George Lombard Jr. | SS |
| Jazz Chisholm Jr. | 2B |
| Austin Wells | C |
| Jose Caballero | 3B |
This lineup still has some good pieces in it. Ben Rice has had a breakout year, Cody Bellinger is a well-rounded star, and trails only Yordan Alvarez and Pete Crow-Armstrong, the AL and NL MVP favorites, with a .532 slugging percentage. If Jazz Chisholm Jr. can return from the IL looking like the player he's capable of being, the Yankees can score runs.
The problem, though, is that six of the nine hitters in this lineup are left-handed, and most of them are much better against righties than lefties. The Yankees will use guys like Paul Goldschmidt and Amed Rosario against left-handed pitching, but having Heliot Ramos, who has a .672 OPS since being acquired by the Yankees at the deadline, in the No. 3 hole against righties isn't ideal. The Yankees don't have much of a choice with Judge out, though.
Ultimately, with Judge out, this is a team heavily reliant on lineup platoons. It'll be on Aaron Boone to try to push the right buttons in order to get this offense, which has been remarkably inconsistent without Judge, to score runs against (likely) a potent Boston Red Sox pitching staff.
Aaron Judge injury update: Can the Yankees expect their star to return?
What's most frustrating about the Judge injury update is that we have no idea what the injury is. The Yankees, for whatever reason, keep information regarding injuries, particularly to Judge, extremely close to the vest, making it difficult to know when or even if Judge will be back. All we know is that Judge is dealing with what Aaron Boone deems a "moderate" strain.
That doesn't sound good, especially for a player who has had trouble with the same right calf in the past. In the shortened 2020 season, Judge attempted to return from a calf strain in a couple of weeks, but wound up re-aggravating the injury, pushing his return back several weeks. Calf injuries and other soft-tissue ailments are not to be messed with, and can lead to a major setback if rushed through.
Plus, if the injury was minor, wouldn't the Yankees be quick to tell the world that? I'd love to say Judge is a lock to return at some point, but even if the Yankees were to advance to the ALDS, given how little we know and how tricky returns can be from calf injuries, it's probably wishful thinking to assume he'd be back right at the start of a potential ALDS, which is the last thign any New York fan wants to hear.

item.title: [saratogian.com] Yankees Notebook: Jazz Chisholm to return for Tuesday’s night game; Clarke Schmidt avoids disaster

item.description: A flurry of injury news came across for the battered and bruised Bronx Bombers on Tuesday at Yankee Stadium. item.content:encoded:
A flurry of injury news came across for the battered and bruised Bronx Bombers on Tuesday at Yankee Stadium.
While the team is clearly compromised and will likely be missing their best player, Aaron Judge, when the playoffs start on Sept. 29, they will be getting their second baseman back with some time to get ready for the inevitable Wild Card Series vs. the Boston Red Sox.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. is expected to be activated between games on Tuesday as the Bombers begin their four-game set with the Tampa Bay Rays with a day-night doubleheader. Chisholm Jr. has been out since Sept. 8 with a right thumb sprain.
“He should be in a good spot and ready to go,” said manager Aaron Boone. “He’s been hitting now for several days and and throwing the last three or four days, so he should be ready to go.”
The 28-year-old is slashing .232/.312/.403 with 19 homers and 55 RBI in 134 games this season. The impending free agent is expected to resume duties as their starting second baseman, which likely doesn’t bode well for Anthony Volpe’s playing time.
“Obviously, Anthony’s done a good job,” said Boone. “But looking forward to getting Jazz back as well. So, Jazz, I plan on playing Jazz at second in the night game.”
Volpe has performed well since being recalled from Triple-A on Sept. 10, slashing .286/.324/.429 with a homer, seven RBI and four stolen bases. It remains to be seen how he will be utilized and if a platoon scenario between Volpe and Chisholm Jr. is on the table.
CLARKE GOOD
Clarke Schmidt appears to have avoided anything major after experiencing bicep soreness while warming up during Sunday’s loss to the Arizona Diamondbacks.
“Clark is gonna play catch [Tuesday]. He did have some testing and it looks like he’s in a pretty good spot.” Boone said. “But [he’s] gotta throw and see how he is, and then we’ll go from there. … He’s on the active roster for now, but he’s got to play catch and do all those things and see how available he is.”
Schmidt returned from Tommy John surgery on Sept. 16 against the Minnesota Twins. He is expected to play a crucial role out of the bullpen in whatever time the Yankees have in the postseason.
WEATHERS UPDATE
Ryan Weathers (left forearm flexor strain) will throw a side session between games on Tuesday. Weathers exited his start against the Toronto Blue Jays on Aug 22 after feeling discomfort and has not appeared in a game since.
If the southpaw is to return in the postseason, it will very likely be out of the bullpen.

item.title: [yardbarker.com] Rays, Yankees each face clinching scenarios in doubleheader

item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Rays will get two chances to clinch their first American League East title since 2021 when they visit the New York Yankees for a day/night doubleheader on Tuesday.
With a magic number of two over the Yankees, the Rays can seal their fate in the afternoon opener.
Tampa Bay (95-60) has won six of the nine games against New York and owns a six-game lead on the Yankees. New York (89-66) has a magic number of two for clinching the AL's top wild-card spot over the Boston Red Sox.
The Rays, who are seeking their fifth division title, have led the AL East every day since June 27.
Following a 2-7 run last month, Tampa Bay is 19-7 since Aug. 23 and just went 8-1 on a homestand against the Houston Astros, Athletics and Red Sox. It featured three walk-off wins and ended with Sunday's 5-1 win over Boston which saw Chandler Simpson and Jonny DeLuca drive in two runs apiece.
"We knew what we had to do," Tampa Bay pitcher Griffin Jax said. "We wanted to put ourselves in a good place going into New York, make it a little bit easier."
The Yankees play host to the Rays for the first time since Aaron Judge's game-ending two-run homer for a 2-0 victory May 24. Judge returned Sept. 8 after missing 84 games with a fractured rib, played seven games and returned to the injured list with a strained calf.
The Yankees are 48-41 in games Judge has not played and enter the upcoming series after losing two of three at Arizona, including an 8-4 loss Sunday. Rookies George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones hit two of New York's three home runs in the third inning, but Brent Headrick gave up a grand slam to Arizona's Nolan Arenado in the fifth.
"We're going to show up and try to win the games on Tuesday, and then we'll keep going from there," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. "We've been through a lot as a team this year already, and we've answered the bell at the turns. We're looking forward to hopefully playing a good week of baseball and building some momentum going into the postseason."
Nick Martinez (15-4, 2.94 ERA) will start the opener for Tampa Bay followed by Drew Rasmussen (15-5, 2.72) in the second game. Martinez is 3-0 with a 2.43 ERA in his past five starts and 2-2 with a 4.30 ERA in 12 career appearances against the Yankees.
Since allowing six runs in 2 1/3 innings at home against the Yankees on July 9, Rasmussen is 8-0 with a 1.91 ERA in his past 11 starts. He is 4-2 with a 1.87 ERA in 10 career outings against the Yankees.
New York will start Carlos Rodon (6-3, 2.95) in the opener followed by Max Fried (5-4, 2.63).
Rodon is 2-1 with a 2.40 ERA in six starts since returning from the injured list Aug. 18 and is 3-3 with a 3.88 ERA in 10 career starts against the Rays
Fried is 1-0 with a 1.83 ERA in four starts since returning from the injured list Aug. 29 and allowed one run in seven innings last Tuesday at Minnesota. He is 5-0 with a 1.26 ERA in six career starts against Tampa Bay.

item.title: [MLB.com] Judge se perdería la Serie del Comodín por distensión “moderada” en la pantorrilla
item.dc:creator: Bryan Hoch
item.description: NUEVA YORK -- Aaron Judge tiene una distensión de “grado moderado” en la pantorrilla derecha y probablemente se pierda al menos el inicio de la postemporada de los Yankees, según el manager Aaron Boone, quien dijo que el club no planea tener a su capitán activo para una posible Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana contra los Medias Rojas. “Estamos planeando que no sea parte de eso”, dijo Boone el martes. “Pero también estamos en una época del año en la que... obviamente lo forzaríamos un poco
item.content:encoded:
NUEVA YORK -- Aaron Judge tiene una distensión de “grado moderado” en la pantorrilla derecha y probablemente se pierda al menos el inicio de la postemporada de los Yankees, según el manager Aaron Boone, quien dijo que el club no planea tener a su capitán activo para una posible Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana contra los Medias Rojas.
“Estamos planeando que no sea parte de eso”, dijo Boone el martes. “Pero también estamos en una época del año en la que... obviamente lo forzaríamos un poco si eso estuviera en juego. Pero falta una semana para eso. No lo espero, pero tampoco lo descarto”.
Los Yankees han asegurado un pase a la postemporada, pero los Rays pueden amarrar el título del Este de la Liga Americana y el sembrado Nro. 1 de la L.A. con una victoria en cualquiera de los choques de la doble cartelera del martes, lo que obligaría a Nueva York a disputar la Serie del Comodín.
Judge fue ingresado a la lista de lesionados de 10 días el sábado, retroactivo al 17 de septiembre.
Recibió una inyección de plasma pobre en plaquetas en la pantorrilla derecha durante el día libre del lunes y tendrá actividades limitadas durante los próximos días.
“El par de días siguientes no habrá mucho: nada de correr, saltar, cosas así”, indicó Boone.
Durante la serie del club el fin de semana en Phoenix, Judge y Boone fueron vagos sobre la gravedad de la lesión, la cual Judge sufrió durante la serie de la semana pasada frente a los Mellizos.
Judge reveló que la distensión es en el músculo sóleo de su pantorrilla derecha, el cual dijo “es un poco más crucial al correr y batear”.
“He lidiado con distensiones antes y de alguna manera he jugado con ellas, pero esta fue en un lugar diferente donde lo hizo un poco más difícil”, comentó Judge.
Generalmente, una distensión de pantorrilla de Grado 2 toma de tres a seis semanas para recuperarse.
“Si él es capaz de jugar, entonces le daremos esa oportunidad”, señaló Boone.
Judge se perdió la mayor parte del verano con una fractura en la costilla derecha, que se cree sufrió el 26 de abril en Houston. Jugó con la lesión antes de ingresar a la lista de lesionados a principios de junio.
Activado en septiembre sin una asignación de rehabilitación en liga menor, Judge disputó sólo siete compromisos después de ser activado, bateando de 23-4 (.174) con un jonrón. En general, Judge bateó .241/.360/.511 con 18 bambinazos y 41 carreras impulsadas en 66 partidos esta campaña.
“Hemos jugado gran parte del año sin él, y en su mayor parte, hemos hecho un trabajo bastante bueno”, destacó Boone. “Obviamente, siempre quieres a tu mejor jugador disponible. Pero entendemos que tenemos un trabajo que hacer y una expectativa de ganar. Creo que esa expectativa no cambia, con o sin él”.
En otras actualizaciones de lesiones, Boone dijo que los Yankees tienen la intención de activar al infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr. entre los encuentros de la doble cartelera del martes.
El derecho Clarke Schmidt se sometió a estudios de imagen tras necesitar acortar su calentamiento el domingo en Phoenix debido a una molestia en su bíceps derecho.
“Por ahora está en el roster activo, pero tiene que soltar el brazo y hacer todas esas cosas para ver qué tan disponible está”, declaró Boone.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are coming off two straight losses in Arizona to the Diamondbacks, a setback that left them a full six games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League East pennant race.
But the Yankees still have a chance to win the division and with it, the top seed in the AL and a bye out of the Wild card playoff round.
The Yankees and Rays open a four-game, head-to-head series with the first game of a doubleheader Tuesday at Yankee Stadium. With a four-game sweep, the Yankees would take the season tiebreaker and need to win at least two of three against the Baltimore Orioles, while the Rays lose two of three to the Philadelphia Phillies to close out the regular season.
Before Game One of the twin bill, the Yankees announced a decision on how they will utilize veteran first basinal Paul Goldschmidt.
Goldschmidt is out of the New York Yankees lineup for a third straight game, sidelined again by a stark platoon split against right-handed pitching.
The pattern has held all September, and it likely has fans wondering about how much longer the 39-year-old holds even a part-time role with October two weeks away.

Boone's Platoon Explains Goldschmidt Sit
Aaron Boone's lineup card for Tuesday's series opener against Tampa Bay leaves Goldschmidt out again, extending a run that traces back to Saturday. He started Friday against left-hander Eduardo Rodriguez in Arizona and went 1-for-4 with a walk and two runs, then sat both weekend games against right-handers Brandon Pfaadt and Corbin Burnes. That's three benchings in the last three games against right-handed starters.
Why? Goldschmidt has produced an elite 1.006 OPS against lefties this season but an anemic a .572 mark versus right-handers, a gap wide enough that Boone starts Ben Rice at DH and Luis García Jr. at first whenever a right-hander pitches. An Athletic report on the lineup moves after Aaron Judge's calf strain named Goldschmidt and Heliot Ramos as the bats Boone leans on against lefties, with García handling the right-handed side.
Nick Martinez, Tuesday's Tampa Bay starter, has largely dominated Goldschmidt in his career. The former National League MVP is 2-for-10 with four walks and two strikeouts against Martinez, and he is 0-for-13 with four strikeouts in his last three meetings with the right-hander since 2024. Martinez enters at 15-4 with a 2.94 ERA this year, and beat the Yankees in the Bronx in May, giving Boone both the season splits and the head-to-head history pointing toward a Goldschmidt benching.
Tuesday's day-night doubleheader against two more right-handed Rays starters gives Boone an easy excuse to sit the 39-year-old.

| 2 | Jonathan Aranda | 1B | .277 | .440 |
| 3 | Junior Caminero | 3B | .277 | .529 |
| 4 | Liam Hicks | C | .288 | .440 |
| 5 | Chandler Simpson | LF | .309 | .360 |
| 6 | Jonny DeLuca | CF | .259 | .410 |
| 7 | Victor Mesa Jr. | RF | .251 | .502 |
| 8 | Ben Williamson | SS | .244 | .328 |
| 9 | Richie Palacios | 2B | .234 | .377 |
| Lineups confirmed. Season stats shown (AVG / SLG). Umpire: Sean Barber • Weather: 63°, Wind 13 mph • O/U: 7 Runs • Line: TB +112 / NYY -135. | | | | |
Goldschmidt's Future in New York
Goldschmidt turns free agent again this winter, and the Yankees have made no public commitment either way. A cheap return as a lefty-masher and clubhouse mentor remains plausible given Rice's grip on first base, and his credentials, a 2022 NL MVP award, seven All-Star selections, four Gold Gloves and five Silver Sluggers still makes him a name teams will inquire about this winter.
First base belongs to Rice, who has grown into an everyday role with 39 home runs and 95 RBI this season, pushing Goldschmidt into a complementary, short-side platoon job. That role fits the final stretch of a one-year, $4 million contract that can grow by $500,000 at each of four plate-appearance thresholds, according to Spotrac, a modest deal compared with the $12.5 million he earned in his first Yankees season a year earlier.

item.title: [New York Daily News] Yankees facing questions about their infield heading into MLB playoffs
item.dc:creator: Peter Sblendorio
item.description: For the third time in five such games, lefty-swinging Yankees third baseman Ryan McMahon was out of the lineup against a right-handed starter to open Tuesday’s doubleheader. In all three instances, righty-swinging José Caballero started at third base instead. Manager Aaron Boone chalked Tuesday afternoon’s decision up to Tampa Bay Rays starter Nick Martinez having reverse splits — meaning he’s actually tougher against lefties — and said McMahon would start the nightcap against a more traditional
item.content:encoded:
For the third time in five such games, lefty-swinging Yankees third baseman Ryan McMahon was out of the lineup against a right-handed starter to open Tuesday’s doubleheader.
In all three instances, righty-swinging José Caballero started at third base instead.
Manager Aaron Boone chalked Tuesday afternoon’s decision up to Tampa Bay Rays starter Nick Martinez having reverse splits — meaning he’s actually tougher against lefties — and said McMahon would start the nightcap against a more traditional righty in Drew Rasmussen.
That would also allow the sure-handed McMahon to play defense on a night Max Fried, who regularly elicits grounders to third base, was starting for the Yankees.
But as McMahon continues to struggle, this is a trend to watch with the MLB postseason rapidly approaching.
“I want to be playing them both and getting them both regular reps,” Boone said before Tuesday’s first game, “so [it was] more just picking what game I wanted to play Caballero.”
Entering Tuesday, McMahon was hitting just .150 with a .402 OPS and no home runs since Sept. 1, when he returned from the injured list for a left thumb sprain.
Overall, he is batting .208 with 10 homers and a .618 OPS.
While his season-long numbers against right-handed pitchers (.639 OPS) are superior to his stats against lefties (.518 OPS), McMahon’s offensive production has been modest either way.
Caballero was already the preferred third-base option against left-handed starters, but now he’s seeing more playing time there against right-handers, too.
A utilityman by trade, Caballero began Tuesday with a .237 average, 10 home runs and a .676 OPS against right-handed pitching.
Caballero’s previous two starts against right-handers came on Sunday against Arizona’s Corbin Burnes, whose splits are fairly even for his career, and last week against Minnesota’s Bailey Ober, who is better against righties than lefties.
That means Caballero isn’t only getting chances against right-handed pitchers with reverse splits.
And while McMahon’s calling card is typically his glove, the advanced metrics have not been favorable to the 31-year-old this season.
McMahon entered Tuesday with -1 Defensive Runs Saved and 1 Outs Above Average — down considerably from his 10 DRS and 7 OAA in 2025.
His numbers at third base this year are comparable to those of Caballero, who began the day with 0 DRS and -1 OAA.
Caballero is also much more dynamic on the bases, as he began the doubleheader with 32 stolen bases. However, starting Caballero eliminates the ability to use him as a pinch-runner — an element of his game that makes him a valuable late-inning weapon come October.
Third base isn’t the Yankees’ only infield position with some uncertainty.
Since being replaced at shortstop by George Lombard Jr. and recalled from Triple-A, Anthony Volpe has performed admirably as the Yankees’ second baseman.
The righty-hitting Volpe began Tuesday hitting .286 with a .753 OPS since being recalled on Sept. 10. He had been worth 1 DRS and 1 OAA at second base over that small sample, too.
Volpe is not going to supplant second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr., who was set to be activated for the second game of the doubleheader after a short IL stint for a right thumb sprain.
But Volpe could challenge for playing time at second base against left-handed pitching, against whom he is hitting .240 with a .680 OPS in the majors this season.
The lefty-swinging Chisholm has endured a down season against lefties, batting .221 with a .654 OPS and a team-worst 35% strikeout rate in those matchups.
“Obviously, Anthony’s done a good job,” Boone said, “but looking forward to getting Jazz back as well.”
The 28-year-old Chisholm wasn’t thrilled last year when the Yankees sat him against left-handed Boston Red Sox ace Garrett Crochet in Game 1 of their Wild Card series.
But with the Yankees likely to face the lefty-heavy Red Sox in the Wild Card round again next week, Boone and company will have more decisions to make at second and third — especially because offense would be at a premium if Aaron Judge (calf) can’t return in time.

item.content:encoded:
BRONX, NY — Jazz Chisholm Jr. is set to be activated from the 10-day injured list following the first game of the Yankees’ doubleheader on Tuesday against the Tampa Bay Rays.
The second baseman missed two weeks after spraining his thumb, and his spot was filled in admirably by Anthony Volpe — the cast-off shortstop who has enjoyed a minor renaissance, of sorts. Entering Tuesday’s action, he had hit safely in six of his 10 games since being called back up from Triple-A, adding a home run and seven RBI. Five of them came in his first game back on Sept. 10 against the Colorado Rockies.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone said that Chisholm is “in a good spot” after hitting and throwing over the past several days. How playing time will shake out remains to be seen.
“We’ll see,” Boone said. “Obviously, Anthony’s done a good job, but looking forward to getting Jazz back as well.”
With the opportunity for playing time seemingly available at third base with Jose Caballero, Ryan McMahon, and Amed Rosario in the mix, Boone had said that “we’ll see” when asked about Volpe potentially moving to the hot corner. Volpe said he has yet to have those conversations with team brass.
It has been a down season for Chisholm, who owns a .715 OPS with 19 home runs and 55 RBI. After a 30/30 season last year, he came into the 2026 campaign hoping to make a run at 50/50.
That did not happen, but getting a healthy Chisholm back who could possibly recapture last year’s spark would provide a significant boost for the Yankees, who are facing the very real possibility of being without Aaron Judge for their Wild Card Series against the Boston Red Sox next week.

item.title: [Pinstripe Alley] New York Yankees vs. Tampa Bay Rays: Carlos Rodón vs. Nick Martinez
item.dc:creator: Peter Brody
item.description: This four-game tilt against the Rays in the penultimate series of the season had the chance to be a blockbuster showdown to decide the division. However, the Yankees losing two out of three to the Diamondbacks removed a lot of the jeopardy from this series, New York now needing to sweep just to avoid being eliminated from the AL East title race and depending on a very unlikely collapse from Tampa in their final series of the season to keep the divisional door the slightest bit ajar. All the same
item.content:encoded:
This four-game tilt against the Rays in the penultimate series of the season had the chance to be a blockbuster showdown to decide the division. However, the Yankees losing two out of three to the Diamondbacks removed a lot of the jeopardy from this series, New York now needing to sweep just to avoid being eliminated from the AL East title race and depending on a very unlikely collapse from Tampa in their final series of the season to keep the divisional door the slightest bit ajar. All the same, this could be a preview of a prospective ALCS showdown, so I expect both teams to come out firing. The first game of today’s doubleheader is a makeup of the rainout from May 23rd.
Carlos Rodón finds himself in the unexpected position of being on the postseason rotation bubble. Cam Schlittler and Max Fried are seemingly locks which would pit Rodón against Gerrit Cole for that final spot if they roll out a three-man rotation. It almost comes down to a style choice at that point — Rodón walks almost three times as many batters as Cole, but surrenders about half as many home runs per nine. He’s a good choice to start a game against the Rays — in six starts against Tampa with the Yankees, Rodón has a 3.69 ERA and 31.3-percent strikeout rate in 31.2 innings. In 15 starts this season, Rodón is 6-3 with a 2.95 ERA (142 ERA+), 3.69 FIP, and 83 strikeouts in 76.1 innings.
The Rays have a maddening habit of transforming other teams’ castoffs into rotation stars. This season’s example is longtime journeyman Nick Martinez, who had pitched as a swingman the previous four years in San Diego and Cincinnati. Martinez owns the lowest walk rate (3.5-percent) of any qualified starter, using deception and precise command to induce soft contact. He’s technically got a six-pitch mix but usually sticks with sinker, changeup, cutter, and four-seamer. In 29 starts, Martinez is 15-4 with a 2.94 ERA (142 ERA+), 3.98 FIP, and 101 strikeouts in 171.1 innings.
This is more or less the Yankees’ go-to lineup for the rest of the regular season with Aaron Judge on the IL. Heliot Ramos and Spencer Jones are both going to get a lot of run out in the outfield, so it was encouraging to see them both hit home runs against the former Cy Young winner Corbin Burnes in their last game. José Caballero gets the start over Ryan McMahon at third and sounded eager to make an impact against the team that traded him to the Yankees at last year’s deadline.
The Rays have their three-headed slugging monster atop lineup and then stack the bottom two-thirds with speed. Junior Caminero is third in MLB with 41 home runs giving him back-to-back 40-HR seasons. Chandler Simpson is MLB’s stolen base leader with 46 and third in batting average at .309, but is the only qualified hitter in baseball without a home run this season.
How to watch
Location: Yankee Stadium - Bronx, NY
First pitch: 1:05 pm ET
TV broadcast: YES, Rays.TV
Radio broadcast: WFAN 660/101.9 FM, WADO 1280 (NYY) | WDAE 95.7 FM, WQBN/1300AM (TB)
Streaming: Gotham Sports App, MLB.tv (out-of-market only)

item.title: [Boston Herald] Yankees reveal Aaron Judge’s status for potential Red Sox playoff series
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Starr
item.description: New York Yankees captain Aaron Judge has a “moderate” calf strain, and is not expected to be available for next week’s Wild Card Series, manager Aaron Boone told reporters on Tuesday morning. “We’re not planning on him being a part of that,” said Boone, who announced that Judge had a Platelet-Poor Plasma injection during Monday’s off-day. (PPP injections are geared toward muscle recovery, as they offer a less inflammatory option than the Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) injections commonly used for jo
item.content:encoded:
New York Yankees captain Aaron Judge has a “moderate” calf strain, and is not expected to be available for next week’s Wild Card Series, manager Aaron Boone told reporters on Tuesday morning.
“We’re not planning on him being a part of that,” said Boone, who announced that Judge had a Platelet-Poor Plasma injection during Monday’s off-day. (PPP injections are geared toward muscle recovery, as they offer a less inflammatory option than the Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) injections commonly used for joint injuries.)
The news is highly relevant for the Boston Red Sox, who are almost certainly set to face their rivals in a rematch of last year’s first round at Yankee Stadium, which the home team took 2-1. Judge went 4 for 11 (.364) with an RBI and two strikeouts in the series.
Judge, 34, is coming off back-to-back American League MVP seasons, and three MVP titles in the last four years. Since the start of 2021 he has hit .306 with a 1.075 OPS, and averaged 49.8 home runs per season (249 in 721 regular-season games).
Injuries cost Judge the majority of 2026, but he remains one of the most fearsome sluggers in the game; his 18 home runs in a mere 66 games would rank fourth on the Red Sox roster this year.

item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge is not expected to be part of the New York Yankees' roster when they begin their wild-card series next week against their likely opponents, the Boston Red Sox, manager Aaron Boone said Tuesday.
The Yankees slugger was placed on the 10-day injured list Friday with a right calf strain. He was eligible to return on Sept. 27, the day of the Yankees' regular-season finale, but now it appears Judge will be out longer.
Regarding Judge's status for the opening round, Boone told reporters, "We're planning on him not being a part of that," and noted that Judge received a PPP injection and is dealing with a "moderate grade" calf strain.
Judge returned Sept. 8 following a three-month IL stint due to a stress fracture in his ribs. Over his seven games back, he went 4-for-23 with 1 home run and 13 strikeouts.
A three-time AL MVP, Judge's 2026 season has been one to forget for the slugger. He got off to a slow start by his standards, slashing only .248/.375/.533 until the Yankees placed him on the IL in early June. Those struggles were partially due to the rib injury, which he reportedly tried to play through for six weeks.
The Yankees have seven games to play and finish the regular season this week at home against the AL East-leading Tampa Bay Rays and Baltimore Orioles. The AL wild-card series is scheduled to begin Sept. 29, and New York is on pace to meet Boston for the second straight postseason.

item.content:encoded:
Aaron Boone shared a more positive update on Jazz Chisholm Jr. ahead of the series opener against the Rays on Tuesday.
The Yankees infielder is to be activated between games of the doubleheader and is expected to return to the lineup for the second game against Tampa Bay. Chisholm Jr. initially landed on the injured list approximately two weeks ago with a right thumb sprain.
He was always expected to return for the postseason, but it will certainly be exciting to see him get some reps before all the chaos begins. Missing Aaron Judge from the Wild Card series, the Pinstripes will need all the power they can get to gain some momentum on offense. This also raises some key questions about who will be put where in the infield once the postseason comes along.

item.title: [amNewYork] Aaron Judge injury latest: Yankees ‘planning’ for slugger to be out for AL Wild Card Series | amNewYork
item.dc:creator: Joe Pantorno
item.description: BRONX, NY — New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone admitted that his team is “planning” not to have superstar slugger Aaron Judge available for the American League Wild Card Series against the Boston Red Sox next week after suffering a “moderate” calf strain. “I have no idea. We’re planning on him not being a part of that,” Boone said before Tuesday’s doubleheader opener against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium. “You hear all the time with injuries, we give ranges: two to four weeks, four to s
item.content:encoded:
BRONX, NY — New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone admitted that his team is “planning” not to have superstar slugger Aaron Judge available for the American League Wild Card Series against the Boston Red Sox next week after suffering a “moderate” calf strain.
“I have no idea. We’re planning on him not being a part of that,” Boone said before Tuesday’s doubleheader opener against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium. “You hear all the time with injuries, we give ranges: two to four weeks, four to six weeks. There are ranges for a reason. We’re at a point in the year where we’d push it a little bit if that was in play. But that’s a week away, so I’m not expecting it, but I’m not ruling it out, either.”
Judge received a PPP (platelet-poor plasma) injection on Monday and will be limited in his activities — mostly just running and jumping — over the next few days.
The 34-year-old captain suffered the injury on Wednesday against the Minnesota Twins, though it is still unclear when exactly it happened. Boone revealed that Judge “felt like it cramped up” when he was picking up the rosin off the pitchers’ mound on his way to the outfield in the first inning.
Not much explanation is needed when going into just how big a hole this leaves in the Yankees’ lineup should Judge not be able to go for the Wild Card Series. The 2026 season has been completely derailed by injuries for a player coming off back-to-back American League MVP Awards. He missed three months due to a fractured rib, then only lasted seven games before this calf strain.
In 66 games, he owned an .871 OPS with 18 home runs and 41 RBI. Even though that is well below recent award-winning paces of his, that would still translate to 44 home runs and 100 RBI over 162 games.
“We’ve played much of the year without him, and so for the most part, we’ve done a pretty good job,” Boone said. “So, guys are used to it. Obviously, you always want your best player in the mix, but we understand we’ve got a job to do and an expectation ot win. And I think that expectation doesn’t change with or without him. We’re expected to go into the series and know we can beat anyone when we play our game.”
Game 1 of the Wild Card Series in the Bronx is scheduled to start on Sept. 29.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Yankees Should Keep Jazz Chisholm Jr. at Second Base Over Anthony Volpe
item.dc:creator: Joseph Randazzo; Unknown
item.description: It was easy for everybody to get ahead of themselves when Anthony Volpe had a big first game back against the Colorado Rockies. Jazz Chisholm Jr. had just gone down, and Volpe delivered a three-hit night capped by a grand slam. At that point, Volpe had gone through a torrid home run streak in the minors, so the thought was that if he replicated it in the big leagues, maybe he could usurp Chisholm. While Volpe's teammates at Triple-A saw the version of him that closely resembled an infield Barry
item.content:encoded:
It was easy for everybody to get ahead of themselves when Anthony Volpe had a big first game back against the Colorado Rockies. Jazz Chisholm Jr. had just gone down, and Volpe delivered a three-hit night capped by a grand slam. At that point, Volpe had gone through a torrid home run streak in the minors, so the thought was that if he replicated it in the big leagues, maybe he could usurp Chisholm.
While Volpe's teammates at Triple-A saw the version of him that closely resembled an infield Barry Bonds, he just wasn't that after that first game. Since then, Volpe has gone 7-for-33. He didn't hit a home run and had just two doubles in that span. In many ways, his .226/.263/.290 slash line is about where he has always been as a big leaguer.
That is why, since Chisholm will be playing in the second game of Tuesday night's doubleheader vs. the Rays, per Chris Kirschner of The Athletic, there's no reason to debate who takes second base. The answer is easily Chisholm. Chisholm hasn't had the best season, but in the postseason, he's more of a threat at the plate and on the basepaths. Chisholm has 19 homers this year with 40 stolen bases. Overall, he's hitting .232/.312/.403 at the plate.
Then, of course, there's the defense. That's why a hitter who's been at or below a 100 wRC+ all year can post a 3.2 WAR, according to FanGraphs. This year, Chisholm also has 12 Outs Above Average at the position, per Baseball Savant.
It does feel like Chisholm is the priority, too, once he's back. According to manager Aaron Boone, when asked about Volpe's status and the possibility of him playing at third base, the focus was on getting Chisholm back.
"We'll see," Boone said of Volpe getting reps at the hot corner, according to the New York Post's Greg Joyce. "First things first, getting Jazz back, and then we'll figure it out as the week unfolds, how I want to play it."
Potential infield configuration against a lefty
If the Yankees face a tough lefty in October and aren't too keen on playing Ryan McMahon, who has a 74 wRC+, and Chisholm, they might have a choice here. They could stick with Chisholm at second and have either Jose Caballero or Anthony Volpe play third base.
They could also have Chisholm go back to third base and have Volpe at second. That way, they keep the better player on the field while also getting a righty at second or third.
With Aaron Judge out, Chisholm could boost the lineup. He's had a tough year, but a big October could make up for some regular-season woes.
Joe Randazzo is a reference librarian who lives on Long Island. When he’s not behind a desk offering assistance to his patrons, he writes about the Yankees for Yankees On SI. Follow him as @YankeeLibrarian on X and Instagram.

item.title: [mlb.com] Judge likely to miss Wild Card Series with 'moderate grade' calf strain
item.dc:creator: Bryan Hoch
item.description: NEW YORK -- Aaron Judge has a “moderate grade” right calf strain and is likely to miss at least the beginning of the Yankees’ postseason, according to manager Aaron Boone, who said the club does not plan to have their captain active for a potential American League Wild Card Series against the Red Sox. “We’re planning on him not being a part of that,” Boone said on Tuesday. “But we’re also at a time of the year where … obviously we’d push it a little bit if that was in play. But that’s a week awa
item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK -- Aaron Judge has a “moderate grade” right calf strain and is likely to miss at least the beginning of the Yankees’ postseason, according to manager Aaron Boone, who said the club does not plan to have their captain active for a potential American League Wild Card Series against the Red Sox.
“We’re planning on him not being a part of that,” Boone said on Tuesday. “But we’re also at a time of the year where … obviously we’d push it a little bit if that was in play. But that’s a week away. I’m not expecting it, but I’m not ruling it out, either.”
The Yankees have clinched a postseason berth, but the Rays can clinch the American League East title and the No. 1 seed in the AL with a win in either game of Tuesday’s doubleheader, which would lock in a Wild Card Series appearance for New York.
He received a platelet-poor plasma (PPP) injection in his right calf during Monday’s off-day and will have limited activities for the next several days.
“The next couple of days will be not much -- no running, jumping, things like that,” Boone said.
During the club’s weekend series in Phoenix, Judge and Boone were vague about the severity of the injury, which Judge sustained during the club’s series last week against the Twins.
Judge revealed the strain is in the soleus muscle of his right calf, which he said “is a little more crucial with running and hitting.”
“I’ve dealt with strains before and kind of played through them, but this was kind of in a different spot where it made it a little bit more difficult,” Judge said.
Generally, a Grade 2 calf strain takes three to six weeks to recover.
“If he’s able to play, then we’ll give him that opportunity,” Boone said.
Activated in September without a Minor League rehab assignment, Judge played just seven games after his reinstatement, going 4-for-23 (.174) with a homer. Overall, Judge batted .241/.360/.511 with 18 homers and 41 RBIs in 66 games this season.
“We’ve played much of the year without him, and for the most part, we’ve done a pretty good job,” Boone said. “Obviously, you always want your best player in the mix. But we understand we’ve got a job to do and an expectation to win. I think that expectation doesn’t change, with or without him.”
"He's on the active roster for now, but he's got to play catch and do all those things to see how available he is," Boone said.

item.title: [Yanks Go Yard] Do you blame Aaron Boone, Brian Cashman, or Rays for Yankees' playoff reality?
item.dc:creator: Adam Weinrib
item.description: The Tampa Bay Rays come to town today for four games in three days. There's a mid-50s chill in the air. Every step you take alternates between dewy grass and dry leaves. It's October baseball, baby. Except, because of the way the standings are situated, the Yankees will likely need to win at least one playoff game to even reach the actual month of October. One Rays win out of four games this week sentences the Yankees to the Wild Card round against the Red Sox, taking place Sept. 29-Oct. 1. That
item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Rays come to town today for four games in three days. There's a mid-50s chill in the air. Every step you take alternates between dewy grass and dry leaves. It's October baseball, baby.
Except, because of the way the standings are situated, the Yankees will likely need to win at least one playoff game to even reach the actual month of October. One Rays win out of four games this week sentences the Yankees to the Wild Card round against the Red Sox, taking place Sept. 29-Oct. 1. That's not how it was supposed to be, but that's how it is.
Do you rage at the sky? The Yankees went through a 5-15 stretch midsummer, then steered out of it nicely, playing some of the best ball in the league in August and September without their Captain. But the Rays were still better. Every time the Yankees won, seemingly so did the Rays. Ditto for losses. They synced their inanity pretty nicely with one another. At one point, the Rays hit a game-tying home run with two outs in the ninth off Mason Miller that was in a Padre's glove and was dropped over the fence. Do you tip your cap, or does the Rays' relentlessness make you angrier?
Aaron Boone, Brian Cashman to blame for Yankees' Wild Card reality?
Do you blame Aaron Boone? The best argument for ditching him with an underwhelming playoff finish is the same as it's always been for me: Time for a new voice. Something has to change. The other arguments ring kind of hollow this year, to be honest. He's manned the ship during a season where injuries should've killed the Yankees, not just derailed them from the pursuit of their primary goal of winning the AL East, but didn't at all. He's done a fantastic job managing an undermanned bullpen.
Do we blame the man who gave him the undermanned bullpen? I lean more in that direction. Brian Cashman's hubris led him to believe the waiver wire and his surplus of injured starting pitchers would build a better bullpen than what was available all offseason/at the trade deadline. We'll see if he's right, but he already failed to account for August wear-and-tear. He crowded the DH room with purpose, forcing Aaron Judge back into right field, then back onto the IL. We needed bats. We didn't necessarily need an added logjam of non-fielders.
Unless the Yankees can somehow sweep a four-game series, including a doubleheader, this week, the Rays will celebrate on their turf. Will it motivate them more than it motivates you, the general fan, some of whom have already counted them out? It had better. Leaving this series with a bad taste in their mouths could pay dividends. It could also end their season before October begins.
This article has been reprinted (with additions and addendums) from the morning edition of the Yanks Go Yard Newsletter. If you'd like to subscribe, sign up here!

item.title: [Pinstripe Alley] Yankees At-Bat of the Week: George Lombard Jr. (9/20)
item.dc:creator: Peter Brody
item.description: Unfortunately, the Yankees effectively pissed away whatever slim chance they had to catch the Rays in the division by losing two out of three to the Diamondbacks, the pitching staff wobbling uncharacteristically in the desert. It was at least encouraging to see the offense mostly carry their weight in the wake of Aaron Judge’s placement on the IL with a right calf strain. The biggest fireworks of the series came in the rubber game loss, three home runs in the third off former NL Cy Young winner
item.content:encoded:
Unfortunately, the Yankees effectively pissed away whatever slim chance they had to catch the Rays in the division by losing two out of three to the Diamondbacks, the pitching staff wobbling uncharacteristically in the desert. It was at least encouraging to see the offense mostly carry their weight in the wake of Aaron Judge’s placement on the IL with a right calf strain. The biggest fireworks of the series came in the rubber game loss, three home runs in the third off former NL Cy Young winner Corbin Burnes momentarily giving them the lead. We’ll look at the middle of those home runs, a two-run blast from George Lombard Jr., on At-Bat of the Week.
We join Lombard with two outs in the top of the third in the rubber game in Arizona on Sunday. Heliot Ramos tied the game with a two-out solo shot two batters earlier and Luis García Jr. kept the inning alive with a single. Wavering with his command from the first batter but particularly this inning, the Yankees need to keep up the pressure and bury Burnes.
Burnes starts this AB like he does many others, with his bread and butter cutter.
Lombard’s swing is pretty much on time to this 92 mph cutter. However, he’s a tick underneath it and fouls it back to the screen.
Burnes apparently likes the way that pitch comes out because he tries to nail the exact same spot with another cutter.
This is no longer the dominant version of Burnes that won the 2021 NL Cy Young award with Milwaukee by painting the corners with upper-90s cutters. Multiple serious arm injuries have limited him to just over 75 innings since signing a six-year, $210 million free agent contract with the Diamondbacks following the 2024 season and robbed him of his top end velocity. This is apparent in just his third start of the year, his cutter averaging just 91 mph and with none of the sharp command of his peak years. Nonetheless, he’s still able to beat Lombard up in the zone with the last two cutters. Both swings have been underneath, telling me that Lombard hasn’t quite figured out the movement profile of the pitch and how it doesn’t drop as much as you might expect.
After hitting the same spot with two straight cutters to jump quickly ahead, 0-2, it’s a perfect time to tunnel a curveball down the same aiming point as the first two pitches of the AB, which should be almost impossible for Lombard not to chase.
The logic is sound but the execution not so much. This pitch exits Burnes’ hand way lower than the first two cutters. Lombard is surely cognizant of a possible breaking ball below the zone for the strikeout here and therefore is able to take this ball in the dirt without much of a flinch.
Burnes must not love the way that curveball came out because he immediately switches back to the cutter. It’s a pitch he’s been able to command in this AB and one that Lombard has not shown he can hit yet.
Burnes yanks this cutter low and away for another straightforward take from Lombard.
After a poorly executed curveball immediately followed by a cutter in a strikeout count, Burnes might have Lombard thinking that another cutter is coming, so he has a second attempt at a curveball below the zone.
Once again, Burnes mis-executes the curveball badly, looping this one high and inside for ball three and another automatic take from Lombard.
Lombard has done well to fight back from 0-2 down to a full count, though he wasn’t put under too much stress by any of Burnes’ attempted strikeout pitches. He likely knows he can hunt a cutter in the zone as Burnes won’t want to put another runner on with two outs and Spencer Jones due up.
As Joe Girardi has said multiple times on the broadcast, a hanging cutter is the best pitch to hit because it runs right into the barrel of your bat. Lombard got a hanger and he did not miss it, demolishing this middle-middle cookie to left for a no-doubter two-run blast. I’ll be honest, I did not know Lombard had this kind of pop. This is 109 mph, 424 feet — the second-hardest-hit ball and by far the longest home run of his young career.
Here’s the full AB:
It’s been really cool to watch Lombard adjust to the Major League level in real time. In this AB specifically, Lombard adjusted his swing path mid-AB to make sure that he stayed on top of an in-zone cutter after swinging underneath a pair. After bursting onto the scene his first two or so weeks post-debut, Lombard like every other big leaguer experienced the growing pains of the league making adjustments. He endured a rocky error streak with the glove and saw the hits dry up, leading to a much needed rotation out of the starting lineup for a day here and there. This apparently allowed him to reset, because he has looked way more sound with the glove and isn’t chasing nearly as much over the last ten days. He’ll need to keep making these adjustments throughout his career, and the ability to do so early in one’s rookie season is a good omen for the future.

item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge volvió a encender las alarmas en los New York Yankees después de sufrir una nueva lesión que lo mandó nuevamente a la lista de lesionados, apenas unos días después de regresar tras una larga ausencia.
La situación genera preocupación en New York, pues el pelotero presenta una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha y ahora existe la posibilidad de que no vuelva a disputar un encuentro durante lo que resta de la temporada.
Aaron Judge vuelve a quedar fuera por lesión
Judge fue colocado nuevamente en la lista de lesionados después de presentar molestias durante el encuentro ante los Minnesota Twins. El problema físico fue confirmado posteriormente mediante estudios médicos.
El regreso del capitán había ocurrido el pasado 8 de septiembre, después de permanecer fuera durante más de tres meses por una fractura en las costillas. Sin embargo, solo pudo disputar siete encuentros antes de volver a quedar fuera.
El momento de la lesión complica todavía más el panorama, ya que Judge podría ser elegible para regresar hasta el 27 de septiembre, cuando los Yankees estarán prácticamente en el cierre de su calendario de temporada regular.
Crece la preocupación en los Yankees
De acuerdo con reportes citados por medios estadounidenses, existe una posibilidad importante de que Judge no vuelva a jugar durante esta temporada. La situación también pone en duda su participación en la postemporada.
El propio jugador mantiene la intención de regresar para los playoffs, aunque todavía no existe un calendario definido para su recuperación. Los Yankees tendrán que esperar la evolución de la lesión antes de tomar una decisión.
La ausencia de Judge representa un problema para New York, especialmente porque el capitán es una de las principales figuras ofensivas del equipo. Ahora, los Yankees deberán esperar para saber si podrá regresar a tiempo para octubre.

item.title: [Yanks Go Yard] Red Sox platoon issues could play right into Yankees hands in potential playoff tilt
item.dc:creator: Stephen Parello
item.description: The New York Yankees' hopes for a deep playoff run took a huge hit when Aaron Judge landed on the IL with a strained calf. Judge says that he'd like to be back in time for the start of the playoffs, but refused to lay out a timeline. While Giancarlo Stanton and his calf strain that never ends (it goes on and on, my friends) is a special case, depending on the severity, this can be a tricky injury. New York's playoff journey is most likely set to begin with a matchup against the archrival Boston
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees' hopes for a deep playoff run took a huge hit when Aaron Judge landed on the IL with a strained calf. Judge says that he'd like to be back in time for the start of the playoffs, but refused to lay out a timeline. While Giancarlo Stanton and his calf strain that never ends (it goes on and on, my friends) is a special case, depending on the severity, this can be a tricky injury.
New York's playoff journey is most likely set to begin with a matchup against the archrival Boston Red Sox. Missing Judge, or having him in a diminished capacity, will be a big blow, but there is still an advantage that the Yankees can leverage.
Several key Red Sox bats are left-handed hitters. Last season, Boston employed a lefty-mashing platoon duo of Rob Refsnyder and Romy Gonzalez to protect those hitters and neutralize any advantage southpaws might hold over them.
However, this year is a different story, as Refsnyder bolted to the Mariners and then retired after a putrid performance led to him being cut, and Gonzalez missed much of the season recovering from shoulder surgery and is currently in Triple-A.
Boston's new lefty-mashing crew has taken some hits lately. Eli White is done for the season with a torn ligament in his right foot. Andruw Monasterio has a .798 OPS against lefties this season, but he's cooled substantially with a .115/.179/.115 line against left-handed pitching since August 1. Jahmai Jones struggled mightily earlier in the season with the Tigers, heated up once picked up by the Red Sox and then slowed back down with a 3-for-18, eight-strikeout performance to begin September.
Yankees are set up to take advantage of Red Sox's recent platoon struggles with Max Fried, Carlos Rodon
The Red Sox's platoon issues play right into the Yankees' hands with Max Fried and Carlos Rodón lurking in the playoff rotation. Fried has battled injuries, but when he's been on the mound, he's been dominant. Seeing him go seven strong in his September 15 start against the Minnesota Twins was a great sign that he's going to be at full strength in time for October.
Rodón is a different case. His velocity drop against the Twins was concerning, but he did rebound later in the start and began pumping 95-plus heat. Overall, though, he doesn't get enough credit for how solid he's been as a Yankee. Most fans' opinions are colored by how his tenure began, but over his last 61 starts in pinstripes, he has a 3.04 ERA.
If Tim Hill can get back on track (outcome hazy, ask again later), the advantage will only grow as the New York can match up following their right-handed starters and later in the game.
There might be a couple of other advantages that the Yankees can exploit. Aroldis Chapman is dealing with a lat issue that hasn't landed him on the IL, but could make him vulnerable. Meanwhile, Willson Contreras was hit by a pitch and suffered a hand injury on September 17 against the Texas Rangers. While X-rays were negative and the hand doesn't appear to be fractured, it could carry over and impact his ability to be a threat at the plate.
The Yankees will need every advantage they can get given Judge's uncertainty. If this matchup comes to fruition, they'll be fortunate enough that the Red Sox are dealing with a number of issues of their own that New York can exploit.

Does nothing for their reputations. And certainly gives no thoughts to their fan base. I could get it if this was a high-minded defense of HIPAA rights. But this feels tied up in paranoia and gripes. And, again, cares not a whit about the paying customer. Because Judge and his bosses should read this sentence with the utmost sincerity with whic
item.content:encoded:
The Yankees and Aaron Judge have two basic public postures when it comes to his injuries — dissembling and disrespectful.
It lowers both team and player. Does nothing for their reputations. And certainly gives no thoughts to their fan base.
I could get it if this was a high-minded defense of HIPAA rights. But this feels tied up in paranoia and gripes. And, again, cares not a whit about the paying customer.
Because Judge and his bosses should read this sentence with the utmost sincerity with which it is offered: I personally don’t care what the status of his current injury is, except to the extent that I would always prefer all the best players play since that usually provides a more enjoyable sport to cover.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees' playoff picture, Aaron Judge update and potential rotation
This wasn’t how the Yankees wanted to move into the regular season’s final week, with a four-game set against Tampa Bay.
Beginning with Tuesday’s day-night doubleheader, they’ll need to sweep the AL East leaders just to prevent the Rays from spilling champagne inside Yankee Stadium’s visiting clubhouse.
And there’s uncertainty surrounding Yankees captain Aaron Judge’s availability next week – the start of postseason − due to a right calf strain.
“We’ve been through a lot as a team this year already and we’ve answered the bell at mostly all the turns,’’ Yanks manager Aaron Boone told reporters, including the YES Network, after Sunday’s 8-4 loss at Arizona.
“(We’re) looking forward to hopefully playing a good week of baseball and building some momentum going into the postseason.’’
Here’s a look at the Yankees’ week ahead:
Yankees vs Rays with AL East race nearing its end
In winning 12 of their last 15 games, the Rays (95-60) have opened a six-game divisional lead on the Yanks (89-66).
On the verge of its first AL East title since 2021, Tampa Bay could clinch it with one win on a long Tuesday in the Bronx.
Tuesday’s opener has Rays right-hander Nick Martinez (15-4, 2.94) scheduled to oppose lefty Carlos Rodon (6-3, 2.95), with righty Drew Rasmussen (15-5, 2.72) vs. lefty Max Fried (5-4, 2.63) in the nightcap.
The Yanks are scheduled to start Gerrit Cole on Wednesday and Cam Schlittler on Thursday.
In the wider picture, Boone acknowledged the need to prep for next week, which includes giving important bullpen arms like Brent Headrick and Paul Blackburn some added rest.
“You’ve got to make sure guys are in a good spot going in (to postseason),’’ Boone told reporters, speaking generally on Sunday.
“But we’re going to show up and try to win the games on Tuesday.’’
Aaron Judge injury update
Judge’s availability for the first playoff round remains a mystery.
This past weekend, Judge told reporters: “I’d like to be back by the postseason. That’s definitely the plan.’’
Judge said he’s played through minor calf strains before, but this current injury to the soleus muscle is a more problematic spot.
So, this will be a key week of treatment and testing to see if Judge could be available in any capacity for a first-round playoff series.
Yankees injury news as Jazz Chisholm Jr. might return
Sidelined since Sept. 9, lefty-hitting second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. (right thumb sprain) could be activated from the injured list to start the Tampa Bay series.
Though he’s unlikely to be activated this week, lefty reliever Ryan Weathers (flexor strain) could find himself on a playoff roster next week in a bullpen capacity.
On the IL since Sept. 5, center fielder Trent Grisham (strained right hamstring) has progressed in his running and is also a possible postseason choice.
Recovered from Tommy John surgery rehab, right-hander Clarke Schmidt developed cramping in his right biceps area while warming up Sunday.
Schmidt did not enter the game, telling reporters it was “more precautionary…especially with the playoffs coming up,’’ in what could be an important relief role.
Initial testing revealed no shoulder or elbow issues, but Schmidt planned to be examined by the team physician Monday.
Schmidt called it “frustrating,’’ but feels “in the grand scheme, we’ll be out there soon.’’
How Yankees' playoff rotation might look
With the likelihood of the Yanks hosting a best-of-three Wild Card series beginning Tuesday, they'd have Cam Schlittler ready on regular rest vs. Boston in Game 1.
But that might not be how the Yankees set things up.
Gerrit Cole would be on one extra day of rest if he's the Game 1 choice, or the Yanks could give the ball to Max Fried with nearly a full week of rest. It's been one month since Fried's return from a second elbow bone bruise this season.
Carlos Rodon could be on a Wild Card roster in an emergency or long relief capacity, or he might be saved to start Game 1 or 2 of a best-of-five Division Series.
CC Sabathia to be honored at Yankee Stadium
Prior to Saturday night's game against the Orioles, CC Sabathia's No. 52 will be retired in a ceremony at Yankee Stadium.
He'll be the 24th Yankees player or manager so honored and the first since Paul O'Neill, who had his No. 21 retired in August 2022.

item.title: [thebiglead.com] Why the Yankees can overcome concerning Aaron Judge development in the MLB playoffs
item.dc:creator: Miracle Dimwesh
item.description: Aaron Judge’s latest injury has created another major question for the New York Yankees heading into the MLB playoffs. Judge landed on the 10-day injured list Saturday with a right calf strain after returning from a lengthy absence earlier this month. The Yankees have not provided a timetable for his return, leaving his availability for October unclear. There is no replacing Judge’s presence in the lineup. Still, New York has one major reason to believe it can survive without its captain: a star
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge’s latest injury has created another major question for the New York Yankees heading into the MLB playoffs.
Judge landed on the 10-day injured list Saturday with a right calf strain after returning from a lengthy absence earlier this month. The Yankees have not provided a timetable for his return, leaving his availability for October unclear.
There is no replacing Judge’s presence in the lineup. Still, New York has one major reason to believe it can survive without its captain: a starting rotation capable of controlling games in October.
Yankees can lean on their starting rotation
The Yankees’ pitching staff has given the team a foundation strong enough to withstand another stretch without Judge.
Cam Schlittler has emerged as the biggest reason for that confidence. The second-year right-hander entered his final regular-season starts with a 14-6 record and a 1.95 ERA, establishing himself as the Yankees’ top postseason pitching option.
Max Fried has also been excellent, carrying a 2.63 ERA through 19 starts. Gerrit Cole has provided another experienced arm with a 3.63 ERA and 123 strikeouts in 21 starts.
Carlos Rodón gives New York another left-handed option. He has also pitched well since returning from his elbow injury, allowing two runs over six innings in his most recent start against Minnesota.
That combination matters in the postseason. If the Yankees can consistently get quality starts, they do not need their offense to produce at the same level every night.
Mark DeRosa sees a path without Judge
MLB Network analyst Mark DeRosa made a similar point when discussing Judge’s injury and the Yankees’ postseason outlook.
“Concern level for Aaron Judge’s injury and the Yankees? Can they overcome it? Yes. They’re built on the strength of their starting rotation,” DeRosa said.
DeRosa also acknowledged the obvious issue. The Yankees need Judge’s presence in the lineup when October arrives, but their pitching gives them another way to win games.
That was already evident during Judge’s earlier absence. He missed more than three months with a rib injury, yet New York still reached the postseason.
The Yankees have already secured a playoff spot, but they still have important games remaining against Tampa Bay. Their final week will help determine their postseason position.
Judge’s return would obviously change the Yankees’ ceiling. But if he cannot make it back in time, New York has something many teams would want in October: multiple starting pitchers capable of taking control of a playoff game.
For the Yankees, that could be the difference between simply surviving Judge’s absence and remaining a serious postseason threat.

item.description: By NOAH TRISTER AP Baseball Writer Justin Verlander and Max Scherzer were together on some memorable Detroit teams before moving on and winning championships elsewhere. Will they eventually enter the Hall of Fame as part of the same class? The first question is whether both will retire after this season.
