item.content:encoded:
By NOAH TRISTER AP Baseball Writer
Justin Verlander and Max Scherzer were together on some memorable Detroit teams before moving on and winning championships elsewhere.
Will they eventually enter the Hall of Fame as part of the same class?
The first question is whether both will retire after this season. The 43-year-old Verlander has already announced this is his final year. He’s made only one start in a reunion season with the Tigers, although Detroit fans are hoping he can return for another this coming week.
Scherzer’s future is less clear. The 42-year-old right-hander is slated to start Tuesday at Baltimore as the Blue Jays try to keep their flickering playoff hopes alive, but Scherzer has posted ERAs over 5.00 both this season and last. He’s on a one-year contract with Toronto.
Some other prominent players may also have made — or might be making — their last appearances in the major leagues. Trey Mancini signed a one-day contract to retire with the Orioles and was celebrated this past weekend in Baltimore. Andrew McCutchen and Carlos Santana, both 39, were released last month. Craig Kimbrel, now 38, has pitched for 10 different big league teams in the last six seasons.
Paul Goldschmidt is 39, but his team — the New York Yankees — is heading to the playoffs. And he may be more important than expected if Aaron Judge is out.
With a lockout possible after this season, there could be some retirements we don’t anticipate. Rick Sutcliffe, Bo Jackson and Hall of Famer Goose Gossage, for example, never played again after the 1994 strike but didn’t actually retire until the following year.
Trivia time
Who is the most recent player voted into the Hall of Fame by the BBWAA whose primary team was the Tigers? (The drought is likely to end soon with Miguel Cabrera and then Verlander.)
Performance of the week
Angel Martínez homered from both sides of the plate and had four hits in Cleveland’s 12-6 win over the Athletics on Saturday night. The Guardians have won five straight and are closing in on a postseason spot. They have a one-game lead over the Chicago White Sox atop the AL Central, and it’s another three games back from the White Sox to Toronto and Houston in the race for the last wild card.
In the National League, Philadelphia leads Arizona by four games for the final wild card, so anyone rooting for chaos this coming week may be disappointed.
Comeback of the week
Detroit was down 8-2 in the fifth inning Friday night before scoring nine unanswered runs to win 11-8 over the White Sox. Kevin McGonigle hit a three-run triple, and both Hao-Yu Lee and Riley Greene added two-run homers during the comeback. Detroit’s win probability was down to 3.2% in the fourth inning according to Baseball Savant.
That’s the only game the Tigers have won out of their last five. They’ve been eliminated from the playoff race, the end of a frustrating season in which nothing seemed to go as planned.
Team of the week
The Los Angeles Dodgers and San Diego Padres both went 6-1, with the Dodgers posting the superior run differential. A three-game sweep of San Francisco leaves the Dodgers four games ahead of Atlanta for the second bye in the National League as they try for a third consecutive World Series title.
There are still health concerns for the Dodgers, with Shohei Ohtani on the injured list and Blake Snell having left his last start after one inning.
Los Angeles did get Edwin Diaz back, and he threw scoreless innings on back-to-back days Friday and Saturday.
Trivia answer
Al Kaline, who was inducted in 1980.
George Kell, Hal Newhouser, Jim Bunning, Sparky Anderson, Jack Morris and Alan Trammell have been elected since then with the Tigers as their primary team, but they weren’t voted in by the BBWAA.
___

item.title: [marca usa] Gran preocupación por Aaron Judge: “Existe una fuerte posibilidad de que no vuelva a jugar esta temporada”
item.dc:creator: Jose Rodriguez
item.description: - MLB. Dave Roberts sobre Shohei Ohtani: “Hay una buena posibilidad de que lo veamos en la próxima serie” - MLB. item.content:encoded:
- MLB. Dave Roberts sobre Shohei Ohtani: “Hay una buena posibilidad de que lo veamos en la próxima serie”
- MLB. Aaron Judge desata la preocupación tras abandonar el juego por una lesión repentina días después de volver a MLB
Los New York Yankees recibieron otro duro golpe en la recta final de la temporada después de verse obligados a colocar nuevamente a Aaron Judge en la lista de lesionados (IL), apenas una semana después de su regreso tras una fractura en las costillas que lo mantuvo fuera durante 60 días.
El capitán de los Yankees ahora enfrenta una distensión en la pantorrilla. Aunque es elegible para volver cuando solamente resten un par de partidos de temporada regular, todavía existe incertidumbre sobre si el equipo decidirá activarlo.
Con Nueva York ya clasificado a la postemporada, la organización enfrenta una decisión clave en los próximos días: arriesgar el regreso de su máxima estrella o darle más tiempo de recuperación pensando en los playoffs.
Aaron Judge podría no volver a jugar esta temporada
El panorama, sin embargo, no luce alentador. El periodista Joel Sherman, de The New York Post, considera que existe una posibilidad real de que Judge no vuelva a disputar un partido este año, incluso si los Yankees avanzan lejos en la postemporada.
“Existe una posibilidad bastante fuerte de que Aaron Judge no vuelva a jugar esta temporada”, aseguró Sherman recientemente.
Aunque las palabras del reportero no representan una confirmación definitiva, sí funcionan como una señal de alerta para los Yankees, quienes podrían llegar a octubre sin su principal referente ofensivo.
La parte positiva para Nueva York es que el equipo ya pasó gran parte de la temporada adaptándose a jugar sin su estrella. Aunque las aspiraciones de Serie Mundial reciben un duro golpe sin Judge en la alineación, el roster ha demostrado que puede competir incluso sin su capitán.
¿Qué dijo Aaron Judge sobre su lesión?
El capitán de los Yankees no ocultó su frustración después de regresar nuevamente a la lista de lesionados el sábado. Aunque evitó dar detalles sobre la gravedad de su distensión en la pantorrilla derecha, Judge dejó claro que mantiene la esperanza de estar disponible para la postemporada.
“Me gustaría estar de regreso para los playoffs. Ese es definitivamente el plan. Es la lista de lesionados de 10 días, así que el décimo día probablemente sea el último partido de la temporada regular. Ya veremos. Realmente no tengo respuestas sobre algún calendario o algo por el estilo”, explicó Judge.

item.title: [MLB.com] Rays y Yankees se preparan para su serie crucial en el Bronx
item.dc:creator: Bryan Hoch; Adam Berry
item.description: NUEVA YORK -- Ha parecido inevitable que la lucha por el Este de la Liga Americana se decidiera esta semana en el Bronx. Los Rays han encabezado la división más competitiva de Grandes Ligas durante gran parte de la temporada y no han cedido el primer lugar de la tabla desde que recuperaron la cima el 27 de junio. Pero los Yankees siempre han estado ahí, amenazando y luego retrocediendo. Pero nunca han estado lo suficientemente lejos como para restarle importancia a lo que podría suceder esta sem
item.content:encoded:
NUEVA YORK -- Ha parecido inevitable que la lucha por el Este de la Liga Americana se decidiera esta semana en el Bronx.
Los Rays han encabezado la división más competitiva de Grandes Ligas durante gran parte de la temporada y no han cedido el primer lugar de la tabla desde que recuperaron la cima el 27 de junio.
Pero los Yankees siempre han estado ahí, amenazando y luego retrocediendo. Pero nunca han estado lo suficientemente lejos como para restarle importancia a lo que podría suceder esta semana.
Pues bien, llegó el momento.
Los Yankees recibirán a los Rays para una serie de cuatro juegos en el Yankee Stadium, comenzando con una doble-cartelera el martes. Gracias a la magnífica estadía de los Rays en casa y a la serie perdida por los Yankees en Phoenix frente a los Diamondbacks, la pregunta ahora es cuánto tiempo más seguirá viva esta lucha.
Los Rays llegaron a Nueva York con 6.0 juegos de ventaja en la división y apenas siete encuentros por disputarse. Una victoria de Tampa Bay eliminará a los Yankees de la lucha por la División Este y los dejará asegurados en un puesto del Comodín de la Liga Americana. Entonces, para que los Yankees tengan alguna posibilidad, deberán completar una barrida de cuatro partidos en tres días.
¿Lo que está en juego? Como dijo una vez Gerrit Cole: “Es mucho”. Entremos en materia.
¿Qué está en juego?
Rays: Ganar apenas un juego les garantizará a los Rays su primer campeonato del Este de la Liga Americana desde el 2021, otorgándoles un pase directo a la Serie Divisional y la ventaja de localía tanto en esa ronda como, si avanzan, en la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Americana. También necesitan una sola victoria para asegurar la serie particular contra los Yankees.
Yankees: El piloto Aaron Boone reconoce que será una “tarea muy difícil” evitar que los Rays celebren con champaña en el Bronx, pero eso es exactamente lo que pretenden hacer. Empezaron la temporada buscando cambiar la narrativa, después de quedarse cortos ante los Azulejos el año pasado. En cambio, están a punto de tener que conformarse nuevamente con un premio de consolación y verse obligados a ganar una serie al mejor de tres juegos.
¿Cómo están alineadas las rotaciones?
Rays: Enviarán a sus mejores dos abridores al montículo para la doble-cartelera del martes. Primero será el derecho veterano Nick Martínez, líder del clubhouse y su fuente más confiable de innings. Tampa Bay tiene marca de 22-7 esta temporada en los juegos iniciados por el cubano-estadounidense. Después, le tocará a Drew Rasmussen, uno de los mejores abridores de la Liga Americana. Los Rays no han perdido una apertura de Rasmussen desde el 9 de julio, con marca perfecta de 11-0 en sus presentaciones desde entonces. Martínez lanzará con un día adicional de descanso, mientras que Rasmussen trabajará con cuatro días de descanso apenas por séptima vez esta campaña. El zurdo Ian Seymour y el derecho dominicano Freddy Peralta estarían alineados para abrir el miércoles y el jueves, respectivamente.
Yankees: Carlos Rodón y Max Fried abrirán los juegos de la doble-cartelera, en ese orden. Ambos han lidiado con lesiones esta temporada, pero están recuperando su mejor nivel en el momento indicado. En tres aperturas de septiembre, Rodón tiene marca de 2-0 con efectividad de 2.08, dejando atrás un episodio de inflamación en el codo izquierdo. Después de ingresar dos veces a la lista de lesionados por una contusión ósea en el codo de lanzar, Fried tiene récord de 1-0 y promedio de carreras limpias de 1.69 en tres aperturas este mes. Cole y Cam Schlittler, favorito para ganar el Premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, seguirán en el tercer y cuarto partidos de la serie, respectivamente.
¿Qué ha estado funcionando bien últimamente para cada equipo?
Rays: ¿Todo? Los Rays acaban de registrar récord de 8-1 durante su última estadía en casa de la campaña regular y han ganado cuatro series consecutivas contra los Bravos, Astros, Atléticos y Medias Rojas. Desde que fueron barridos en una serie de cuatro partidos en el Fenway Park tras la pausa del Juego de Estrellas, tienen marca de 39-18, la mejor de la Gran Carpa desde el 20 de julio. Su pitcheo abridor se ha visto particularmente sólido, con efectividad de 2.81 este mes, sólo detrás de la de los Yankees. Como de costumbre, han encontrado distintas maneras de anotar carreras, incluyendo ataques tempraneros como el del domingo y un par de jonrones para dejar en el terreno al rival por parte del candidato al JMV de la Liga Americana, el dominicano Junior Caminero.
Yankees: De repente, estos Yankees se encuentran apoyándose en la fortaleza de su pitcheo, confiando en que la ofensiva terminará respondiendo. Ben Rice conectó su 39no cuadrangular, la mayor cantidad del equipo, cumpliendo una predicción que Boone hizo durante los Entrenamientos de Primavera. Rice dijo que Boone estaba bromeando con él, quedándose con “uno o dos” por debajo de la cifra que él prefería, así que habrá que estar atentos a Rice mientras busca su 40mo vuelacercas esta semana. Austin Wells ha conectado tres bambinazos en sus últimos seis encuentros, mientras que el puertorriqueño Heliot Ramos ha volado la cerca en sus últimos dos partidos. Podría ser una pieza importante si los Yankees quieren hacerse sentir en octubre.
¿Cuáles son algunas áreas de preocupación que podrían convertirse en un problema esta semana o en la postemporada?
Rays: Muchos jugadores de los Rays han dado un paso al frente, pero el primer bate del equipo, el cubano Yandy Díaz, ha tenido un mes complicado, con línea ofensiva de .229/.286/.357 en septiembre. Él marca la pauta para la alineación, así que obviamente será importante que llegue en su mejor nivel a octubre. Y esto es realmente buscarle la quinta pata al gato, considerando que tiene marca de 3-0 con un salvamento y efectividad de 1.42 este mes, pero Bryan Baker, líder de Grandes Ligas en salvamentos, suma más bases por bolas (cuatro) que ponches (dos) en siete presentaciones durante septiembre. También necesitarán que sea dominante en la postemporada.
Yankees: Más allá del tirón en la pantorrilla derecha de Aaron Judge, un asunto que los Yankees están manejando como si fuera un secreto del estado, comienzan a surgir preocupaciones sobre el estado del bullpen. La velocidad de Brent Headrick ha disminuido y el relevista podría estar mostrando señales de fatiga después de liderar las Mayores con 79 presentaciones. Tim Hill no ha sido la máquina automática de provocar rodados de años anteriores. Michael Fulmer permitió un jonrón que decidió un juego en Arizona. Pero no hay un asunto más importante que demostrar que pueden ganar sin Judge, el motor alrededor del cual gira su ofensiva. Tienen marca de 48-41 sin él, comparada con 41-25 cuando ha estado en acción.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Postemporada MLB: clasificaciones, salud de Ohtani y Judge y premios
item.dc:creator: DAVID BRANDT
item.description: Postemporada MLB: clasificaciones, salud de Ohtani y Judge y premios La postemporada de las Grandes Ligas de Béisbol se acerca rápidamente, con los Dodgers de Los Ángeles en busca de un tercer título consecutivo de la Serie Mundial. item.content:encoded:
Postemporada MLB: clasificaciones, salud de Ohtani y Judge y premios
La postemporada de las Grandes Ligas de Béisbol se acerca rápidamente, con los Dodgers de Los Ángeles en busca de un tercer título consecutivo de la Serie Mundial. Sin embargo, aún está por verse cuánto podrán participar algunas de las mayores estrellas del deporte cuando llegue octubre.
Los Dodgers vuelven a estar entre los mejores equipos de las Grandes Ligas, y tendrán varios retadores en octubre, incluidos los Cerveceros de Milwaukee y los Rays de Tampa Bay. Los tres equipos podrían terminar la temporada regular con 100 victorias o más. Los Ángeles está ahí pese a que la salud del cuatro veces Jugador Más Valioso Shohei Ohtani es motivo de preocupación.
Los Yankees de Nueva York, los Medias Rojas de Boston y los Bravos de Atlanta también han asegurado lugares en la postemporada. El tres veces Jugador Más Valioso de los Yankees, Aaron Judge, lidia con una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha que lo mantendrá en la lista de lesionados al menos hasta el último día de la temporada regular.
La temporada regular termina este domingo y, aunque el cuadro de playoffs de 12 equipos parece estar mayormente definido, hay algunos aspirantes con pocas probabilidades de llegar a la postemporada, y los enfrentamientos específicos están en movimiento.
A continuación, algunas de las cosas a seguir mientras la temporada llega a su fin.
Equipos que pueden asegurar un puesto de playoffs el lunes
Ningún equipo puede asegurar un puesto de playoffs el lunes, ya que la mayor parte de la liga tendrá el día libre.
Hay un partido importante en la Liga Americana, donde los Azulejos de Toronto viajan para enfrentar a los Orioles de Baltimore. Los Azulejos se mantienen apenas en el borde de la pelea en la LA, al iniciar el día a tres juegos del último puesto de comodín.
Lucha en la Liga Americana sigue en duda mientras la Liga Nacional está más definida
Esta temporada ha habido bastante mediocridad en las divisiones Central y Oeste de la LA, lo que ha derivado en carreras por el banderín fascinantes y podría llevar a que un equipo con marca por debajo de .500 llegue a la postemporada.
Los Guardianes de Cleveland (81-75) tienen una ligera ventaja sobre los Medias Blancas de Chicago (80-76) en la Central de la LA, mientras que los Rangers de Texas (78-78) están apenas por delante de los Astros de Houston (77-79) en el Oeste de la LA.
En la Liga Nacional, el cuadro de playoffs está casi definido.
Los Cachorros de Chicago (87-69), Padres de San Diego (87-69) y Filis de Filadelfia (86-70) se disputan posiciones en la carrera por el comodín, pero casi con seguridad llegarán a la postemporada. El único equipo a una distancia relativamente cercana es el de los Diamondbacks de Arizona (82-74), que está a cuatro juegos.
Carreras por el MVP, estadísticas a seguir
Los principales premios de la MLB probablemente no tendrán mucho drama esta temporada.
Ambas carreras por el MVP tienen claros favoritos, con Pete Crow-Armstrong, de Chicago, despegándose rumbo al honor en la LN, mientras que el cubano Yordan Alvarez, de Houston, es la opción probable en la LA, aunque el dominicano Junior Caminero, de Tampa Bay, también ha tenido una temporada fantástica. Alvarez aún tiene una oportunidad de lograr la rara Triple Corona. Lidera la LA en promedio de bateo con .313, pero sus 40 jonrones están a uno de Caminero y sus 99 carreras impulsadas están a seis de las de Pete Alonso, de Baltimore.
Para el premio Cy Young, el lanzallamas de Milwaukee Jacob Misiorowski y el as de Nueva York Cam Schlittler son los favoritos en la LN y la LA, respectivamente.
Las carreras por el Novato del Año también parecen definidas, con Sal Stewart, de Cincinnati, y su temporada de 110 carreras impulsadas como líder en la LN, y Kevin McGonigle, de Detroit, como favorito en la LA.
¿Cuál es el formato de playoffs de la MLB?
Hay 12 equipos que clasifican a la postemporada de la MLB, incluidos seis equipos tanto de la LA como de la LN. Los tres ganadores de división en cada liga reciben las siembras número 1 a número 3, ordenadas por récord de victorias y derrotas. Luego, los tres equipos de comodín reciben las siembras número 4 a número 6, también ordenadas por récord de victorias y derrotas.
Los dos mejores equipos con el mejor récord tanto en la LA como en la LN avanzan automáticamente a la Serie Divisional. Los otros ocho equipos juegan la Serie de Comodines, que es un formato al mejor de tres y comienza el martes 30 de septiembre. Tanto en la LA como en la LN, el sembrado número 6 viajará para enfrentar al sembrado número 3, mientras que el sembrado número 5 va contra el número 4. El sembrado más alto es anfitrión de los tres juegos.
Los ganadores avanzan luego a la Serie Divisional al mejor de cinco, seguida por la Serie de Campeonato de Liga al mejor de siete y una Serie Mundial al mejor de siete entre los ganadores de la LA y la LN.
¿Cuál es el calendario de la postemporada de la MLB?
Ronda de Comodines: 29 de septiembre-1 de octubre (NBC/Peacock)
Serie Divisional: 3-10 de octubre (LA en TBS, LN en FOX/FS1)
Serie de Campeonato: 11-20 de octubre (LA en TBS, LN en FOX/FS1)
Serie Mundial: 23-31 de octubre (FOX)
¿Quiénes son los favoritos para ganar la Serie Mundial?
Los Dodgers (+220) son los favoritos para conquistar un tercer título consecutivo de la Serie Mundial, mientras que los Cerveceros (+600), Yankees (+800) y Rays (+800) son considerados los principales contendientes.
___

item.title: [tsn.ca] The latest on MLB postseason clinches, Ohtani and Judge health updates, awards races and more

item.content:encoded:
Major League Baseball’s postseason is rapidly approaching, with the Los Angeles Dodgers seeking a third-straight World Series title. It remains to be seen how much some of the game’s biggest stars will be able to participate come October, though.
The Dodgers are once again among the best teams in the big leagues, and they’ll have several challengers in October, including the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays. All three teams could finish the regular season with 100 wins or more. Los Angeles is there even though four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani’s health is a concern.
The New York Yankees, Boston Red Sox and Atlanta Braves have also clinched spots in the postseason. The Yankees’ three-time MVP Aaron Judge is dealing with a right calf strain that will keep him on the injured list until at least the final day of the regular season.
The regular season ends this Sunday, and while the 12-team playoff field appears mostly set, there are a few long-shot contenders for the postseason, and specific matchups are in flux.
Here’s some of what to watch as the season comes to a close.
Here’s who can clinch a playoff spot Monday
No team can clinch a playoff spot on Monday with most of the league getting a day off.
There is one important game in the American League, where the Toronto Blue Jays travel to face the Baltimore Orioles. The Blue Jays are hanging on the fringe of the AL race, starting the day three games back of the final wild-card spot.
AL race is murky while NL is more defined
There’s quite a bit of mediocrity in the AL Central and West divisions this season, which has led to some fascinating pennant races and could lead to a sub-.500 team making the postseason.
The Cleveland Guardians (81-75) have a narrow advantage over the Chicago White Sox (80-76) in the AL Central while the Texas Rangers (78-78) are just ahead of the Houston Astros (77-79) in the AL West.
Over in the National League, the playoff bracket is close to set.
The Chicago Cubs (87-69), San Diego Padres (87-69) and Philadelphia Phillies (86-70) are jockeying for position in the wild-card race but will almost certainly make the postseason. The only team within shouting distance is the Arizona Diamondbacks (82-74), who are four games back.
MVP races, stats to watch
MLB’s major awards probably won’t have much drama this season.
Both MVP races have strong favorites with Chicago’s Pete Crow-Armstrong running away with the NL honor while Houston’s Yordan Alvarez is the probable choice in the AL, though Tampa Bay’s Junior Caminero has also had a fantastic season. Alvarez still has a shot at a rare Triple Crown. He leads the AL in batting average at .313 but his 40 homers are one behind Caminero and his 99 RBIs are six back of Baltimore’s Pete Alonso.
For the Cy Young Award, Milwaukee flame thrower Jacob Misiorowski and New York ace Cam Schlittler are the favorites in the NL and AL, respectively.
The Rookie of the Year races also look set with Cincinnati’s Sal Stewart and his 110-RBI season the leader in the NL and Detroit’s Kevin McGonigle the favorite in the AL.
What is the MLB playoff format?
There are 12 teams that qualify for MLB’s postseason, including six teams from both the AL and NL. The three division winners in each league get seeds No. 1 through No. 3, ranked by win-loss record. Then the three wild-card teams get seeds No. 4 through No. 6, also ranked by win-loss record.
The top two teams with the best record in both the AL and NL automatically advance to the Division Series. The other eight teams play in the Wild Card Series, which is a best-of-three format beginning on Tuesday, Sept. 30. In both the AL and NL, the No. 6 seed will travel to face the No. 3 seed while the No. 5 seed goes to No. 4. The higher seed hosts all three games.
The winners then advance to the best-of-five Division Series, followed by the best-of-seven League Championship Series and a best-of-seven World Series between the winners of the AL and NL.
What is the MLB postseason schedule?
Wild Card Round: Sept. 29-Oct. 1 (NBC/Peacock)
Division Series: Oct. 3-10 (AL on TBS, NL on FOX/FS1)
Championship Series: Oct. 11-20 (AL on TBS, NL on FOX/FS1)
World Series: Oct. 23-31 (FOX)
Who are the favorites to win the World Series?
The Dodgers (+220) are the favorites to capture a third straight World Series title while the Brewers (+600), Yankees (+800) and Rays (+800) are viewed as the top contenders.
___
See AP’s full MLB coverage here
David Brandt, The Associated Press

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Aaron Judge Injury: Yankees Impact in Shifting AL Playoff Race
item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy; Unknown
item.description: Over the last few days, Aaron Judge has been the talk of Major League Baseball. Judge is back on the Injured List after returning from the IL for a brief seven-game stint. item.content:encoded:
Over the last few days, Aaron Judge has been the talk of Major League Baseball.
Judge is back on the Injured List after returning from the IL for a brief seven-game stint. Judge has played in just 66 games this season and the biggest question in baseball is whether he will be able to return during the postseason. If Judge is Judge, then the Yankees are built to make a run to the World Series. If Judge doesn't return, all of a sudden the Yankees look like a team that could have a short playoff run. On Monday, Joel Sherman of the New York Post gave an update that will could certainly impact the race.
"There's some strong possibility he doesn't play anymore," Sherman said. "Calf strains are notorious for when they heal, let them heal more because it is a re-injury area of the body."
At this point, the vibes aren't high or pointing towards a return for Judge. Calf injuries are tough. Jim Bowden of The Athletic reported that Judge is dealing with a soleus strain. The playoffs begin in eight days. On Sep. 29, the Yankees will begin a three-game Wild Card series, very likely against the Boston Red Sox.
If Sherman is correct and Judge doesn't return, it completely changes the calculus of the American League playoffs. A healthy Judge balances New York's lineup. Without him, the Yankees are lefty-heavy. Outside of Ben Rice, no other member of the Yankees has hit more than 20 homers as a member of New York this season. Luis García Jr. has 30 total homers, but has hit just seven in a Yankees uniform. The power threat isn't the same without Judge.
The Tide Is Shifting In the American League
New York will have to face off against the Red Sox in a three-game Wild Card series, barring something shocking happening. Even if the Yankees were to win, they would then have to go against the American League-leading Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Division Series. A brutal one-two punch, to say the least.
Without Judge, that arguably should make the Red Sox the favorites in a three-game set. New York's lineup is lefty-heavy. The Red Sox happen to be loaded from a left-handed pitching standpoint. The Red Sox could roll with Payton Tolle and Ranger Suárez in two out of three games. Plus, Garrett Crochet is close to returning in a bullpen role. Imagine a scenario in which the Red Sox start either Tolle or Suárez in a game and then get multiple innings out of a healthy Crochet afterward? That's the worst-case scenario for a Yankees lineup that is full of lefties.
If Boston advances, it would be a toss-up between the Red Sox and the Rays in an ALDS series. Then, either would be the favorite in the American League Championship Series over the Chicago White Sox, Cleveland Guardians or the Texas Rangers. Arguably, the Red Sox should be the favorites in the American League in general right now with Judge out, although it would be close. The Red Sox have been the best team in baseball since the end of June and now the path is a little clearer.
The American League runs through the American League East. If Judge was fully healthy, New York would be the favorites. The Yankees' rotation is electric and this team can seriously put up runs when Judge is at his best. Judge is the most impactful right-handed hitter in baseball. This is a guy who three out of the last four AL MVP awards, including the last two years in a row. When he's on the field, he moves the needle. Without him, the Yankees are still good, but they're not as big a World Series threat.
Patrick McAvoy's experiences include local and national sports coverage at the New England Sports Network with a focus on baseball and basketball. Outside of journalism, Patrick also received an MBA at Brandeis University. For all business/marketing inquiries regarding Fastball On SI, please reach out to Scott Neville: scott@moreviewsmedia.com

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees were forced to place Aaron Judge back on the IL just a week after he returned from the 60-Day IL with a fractured rib.
He’s now on the IL with a calf strain and is eligible to return with just a couple of games left in the regular season, but it’s unclear if the Yankees will go that route.
Either way, with a postseason berth already locked up, the Yankees’ judgment day is rapidly approaching, and rather shortly they will have to make a decision on Judge.
Well, Yankees pundit Joel Sherman isn’t too optimistic that Judge will even play again this season, regardless of how far the Yankees advance.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Josue De Paula Shares Honest Message
Joel Sherman Thinks Aaron Judge May Not Play Again This Season
Joel Sherman recently said (about Judge):
“There’s some strong possibility that Aaron Judge doesn’t play anymore this season”
It’s a very vague statement by Sherman, but certainly a major warning for Judge and the Yankees.
The good thing for New York is they’ve been without their star slugger for so long this season, and while their World Series chances take a significant hit without Judge, it’s not like this currently constructed roster isn’t used to not having him in the order (for this season at least).
There is growing belief that Aaron Judge may be so hurt that it’s not worth sending him out to play if he’s less than 50%.
More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Face Major Free Agency Choice on All-Star Pitcher
More on Aaron Judge’s Importance
If the New York Yankees are going to be without Aaron Judge for the rest of the MLB season, it will be all hands on deck for the rest of the squad.
Things tend to be magnified in the MLB playoffs, so there will need to be big swings from other contributors if the Yankees are going to make a deep run behind perhaps the best pitching staff in the playoffs.
With that being said, even if Judge’s playoff numbers don’t necessarily match his regular-season pace, his being in the batting order completely changes the complexity of how the opposing pitching staff targets the Yankees batters.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Mets Trade Pitch Offloads Mark Vientos to Pirates

item.title: [blogs.fangraphs.com] Untying the Tiebreaker Scenarios, One More Time
item.dc:creator: Jay Jaffe
item.description: With one week to go in the regular season, the playoff field is nearly set in the National League, though it’s anything but settled in the American League, with two of the three division leaders — two different ones since I last checked in — ahead by just one game and those races spilling over into the battle for the third and final Wild Card spot. We’re not going to get any tiebreaker games due to the fun police and the playoff format change put into effect by the 2022 Collective Bargaining Agr
item.content:encoded:
With one week to go in the regular season, the playoff field is nearly set in the National League, though it’s anything but settled in the American League, with two of the three division leaders — two different ones since I last checked in — ahead by just one game and those races spilling over into the battle for the third and final Wild Card spot. We’re not going to get any tiebreaker games due to the fun police and the playoff format change put into effect by the 2022 Collective Bargaining Agreement, but it’s entirely possible a playoff spot — and perhaps even a division title — will be decided on the basis of MLB’s tiebreaker procedures.
Since the situation is simpler in the NL, I’ll start there. The Brewers (98-58) lead the Dodgers (96-60) in the race for the top seed, and own the tiebreaker there on the basis of a 4-3 season series advantage. According to our Playoff Odds, as of Monday at 9 AM, the Braves (92-64) have just a 0.9% chance of bypassing either Milwaukee or Los Angeles. The Brewers — who have a magic number of one to clinch a first-round bye — finish out with a visit to the Phillies (86-70) before coming home to face the Cardinals (76-80), while the Dodgers host the Padres (87-69) for three and then travel to the Giants (62-90), with the Braves hosting the Reds (72-84) and then visiting the Marlins (76-80).
The Padres have taken advantage of a soft spot in their schedule — series against the sub-.500 Nationals, Giants, Rockies, and Marlins, after taking two out of three from the Yankees — to win 13 out of their last 14 games. Not only did that push them past the Diamondbacks (now 82-74), whom they trailed by half a game before the start of the surge, but they’ve tied the Cubs (87-69) for the top NL Wild Card spot, with the Phillies a game behind them. The Phils have been phlailing lately, going 8-10 in September and failing to win a series since beating the Diamondbacks at the start of the month. Their slide gave the Braves enough room to clinch the NL East title on Sunday.
Before turning to the grid involving the four NL teams battling for three Wild Card spots, here’s another look at the tiebreaking procedures:
- Head-to-head records: This is self-explanatory when it comes to two-team tiebreakers, and if they played an odd number of games against each other, which is currently the case if they’re in the same division, then no other steps will be necessary. If more than two teams are involved and they have identical records against each other, then the team with the best combined winning percentage against the other teams within the tie wins the tiebreaker. If it’s still relevant, the remaining two teams are untied by head-to-head records and on down the line.
If more than two teams are involved and they do not have identical records against one another, but one team won its season series against each of the other teams, then that team takes the tiebreaker. Otherwise, it goes in order of combined winning percentage against the other teams they’re tied with, as above. One additional point to add in the event of a tie involving more than two teams: If it has implications for both a division race and a Wild Card race, the division tiebreaker is settled first, on the basis of head-to-head records. For example, if the Rangers and Astros tie atop the AL West and the White Sox finish with the same record but behind the Yankees and Red Sox, the Texas/Houston tiebreaker is settled first.
- Intradivision records: This one is relevant only for two situations — multi-team scenarios where the teams all have the same head-to-head records within the group, or for two Wild Card teams in different divisions. In the latter case, there’s still a good chance they played seven games against each other instead of six.
- Intraleague records: A team’s record against all three divisions in the same league.
- Last half of intraleague games: If a team has played 48 interleague games, then this would be decided based on their winning percentage over the last 57 (half of 114) games against teams in their own league. And if that doesn’t work…
- Last half of intraleague games plus one… or more, as needed: Under the above scenario, this would be decided based on their winning percentage over the last 58 intraleague games, then 59, 60, 61… as many as it takes.
And now, the big board:
| Team | W-L | CHC | SDP | PHI | ARI | Intra |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CHC | 87-69 | — | 5-1 (0,0) | 6-1 (0,0) | 4-2 (0,0) | 26-26 |
| SDP | 87-69 | 1-5 (0,0) | — | 0-6 (0,0) | 5-5 (3,0) | 28-18 |
| PHI | 86-70 | 1-6 (0,0) | 6-0 (0,0) | — | 3-3 (0,0) | 28-24 |
| ARI | 82-74 | 2-4 (0,0) | 5-5 (0,3) | 3-3 (0,0) | — | 28-18 |
The Cubs have a leg up on all of the other contenders here when it comes to the battle for the top Wild Card spot because they took the season series from each one. If they end up in any kind of tie, that advantage will be the difference between them playing the entire best-of-three series at Wrigley Field versus going on the road. The Padres are already on the short end of things with regards not only to the Cubs but also to the Phillies, with their series against the Diamondbacks hanging in the balance. San Diego hosts the Snakes at Petco Park over the regular season’s final weekend to determine who has the upper hand, though by then it may not matter.
Since they split their season series, a Phillies-Diamondbacks tie would be based on intradivision records. Philadelphia doesn’t have any more games against NL East rivals remaining; they host the Brewers and Rays for three-game sets starting on Tuesday. The Diamondbacks, who travel to both Colorado and San Diego, need one more win to clinch the intradivision tiebreaker advantage, but realistically they need a lot more than that to improve their chances. Their Playoff Odds are down to 5.6%.
Back to the Cubs, who host the Marlins for three and then visit the Red Sox (84-72). In the event of a four-team tiebreaker, Chicago would win because they beat all three other teams, and likewise for any three-way tiebreaker that involves them. If there’s any need to go further than that — say, if there were a three-way tie for the top Wild Card spot — after the Cubs it would come down to head-to-head and then intradivision records. A three-way tiebreaker not involving the Cubs would be decided first on combined head-to-head records within the group. Based on current records, the Phillies (.750, 9-3) would have the advantage over the Diamondbacks (.500, 8-8) and Padres (.313, 5-11), and once they’re untied from that knot, an Arizona-San Diego tiebreaker would still come down to head-to-head records.
Turning to the American League, the Rays (95-60) own a six-game lead over the increasingly banged-up Yankees (89-66) — who will be without Aaron Judge for the rest of the regular season due and possibly longer, due to a right calf strain — in the AL East. The two teams have a four-game series in the Bronx starting with a doubleheader on Tuesday. Tampa Bay leads the season series 6-3; a single win would not only seal a potential tiebreaker, it would clinch the division title. Nobody’s going to catch the Rays for the number one seed, either. The Guardians (81-75) took two out of three from the White Sox (80-76) this past week in Cleveland to take over first place in the AL Central. That said, Chicago owns the 7-6 season series advantage for tiebreaking purposes and has the softer schedule ahead; the White Sox visit Kansas City (67-89) for three and then host Colorado (57-99), while Cleveland travels to Boston and then Kansas City for a pair of three-game series. Whichever team wins the AL Central will likely grab the second first-round bye; between the Guardians and White Sox, their odds of doing so are 97.3%.
Meanwhile, the Rangers (78-78) are clinging to a one-game lead over the Astros (77-79), and yes, it’s entirely possible that the winner could be the majors’ first full-season sub-.500 playoff team. Houston won the season series 9-4 and therefore has the tiebreaker in the AL West, but for both teams, it’s all scoreboard-watching the rest of the way. The Astros are on the road against the Mariners (73-83) and A’s (61-95), while the Rangers host the Mets (71-85) for three before finishing with three in Minnesota (73-83).
As for the AL Wild Card, we don’t need to mind the Yankees and Red Sox since they’ve clinched playoff berths and are more or less locked into their spots; one Yankees win or one Red Sox loss will sew up placement as the fourth and fifth seeds, with a rematch of last year’s Wild Card Series slated for the Bronx. For the big board below, I’m including the Guardians and Rangers since it won’t take much to bump either of them into a position where their tiebreakers matter.
| Team | W-L | CLE | CHW | TEX | HOU | TOR | Intra |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLE* | 81-75 | — | 6-7 | 2-4 | 2-4 | 2-4 | 27-22 |
| CHW | 80-76 | 7-6 | — | 4-2 | 2-5 | 5-1 | 31-18 |
| TEX* | 78-78 | 4-2 | 2-4 | — | 4-9 | 6-1 | 23-29 |
| HOU | 77-79 | 4-2 | 5-2 | 9-4 | — | 3-3 | 22-24 |
| TOR | 77-79 | 4-2 | 1-5 | 1-6 | 3-3 | — | 25-24 |
Alas, with the Rangers and Blue Jays finishing their season series on Sunday, none of these teams will face each other again until October, so we’re left with the same four scenarios I outlined a couple of weeks ago, but with the division leads having changed hands.
Scenario 1: Guardians and Rangers win their divisions
If both division leaders maintain their spots, leaving the other three teams vying for the sixth seed, the Astros would have the advantage over the White Sox in a tiebreaker because they won their season series. Because the Astros and Blue Jays split their series, a tie between them would be broken based on intradivision records; right now, the Blue Jays have the advantage, but they have fewer such games remaining (three in Baltimore from Monday to Wednesday, with their final three at home against the Reds), while the Astros, as noted, have six to play against AL West rivals. If the two teams end up with the same intradivision records, the next step would be intraleague records; currently the Astros have the edge, with a .519 winning percentage (56-52) to the Blue Jays’ .495 (55-56).
In the case of a three-way tie, the Astros would prevail, because they went 8-5 (.615) against the other two teams, while the White Sox went 7-6 (.538) and the Blue Jays 4-8 (.333).
Scenario 2: White Sox and Rangers win their divisions
This one would leave a three-team fray between the Astros, Guardians, and Blue Jays. The Astros won their season series against the Guardians, and a potential tie with the Blue Jays would be settled by intradivision or intraleague records as noted above.
In a three-way tie involving combined head-to-head records, the Astros and Blue Jays would tie at .583 (7-5), leaving the Guardians (.333, 4-8) in the dust. The Astros/Blue Jays tiebreaker would then be settled as outlined above.
Scenario 3: Guardians and Astros win their divisions
If the Guardians hold onto their narrow one-game lead, the White Sox would still be in decent shape, as they took the season series from both the Blue Jays and Rangers, so in the event of a three-way tie, Chicago would claim the remaining Wild Card berth.
Scenario 4: White Sox and Astros win their divisions
The Rangers remain sandwiched between the Guardians and Blue Jays record-wise, but they have the tiebreaker advantage over both teams. Because they won their season series against both Cleveland and Toronto, in a three-way tie, they would come out on top.
Undeniably, the situation in both leagues still leaves room for some suspense with regards to who will advance to October. Still, we can hope that as the players and owners hammer out the next CBA during what is likely to be a frigid winter on the labor front, they think long and hard about what’s been lost with the elimination of tiebreaker games. It’s much more fun rooting for chaos than for math.
Brooklyn-based Jay Jaffe is a senior writer for FanGraphs, the author of The Cooperstown Casebook (Thomas Dunne Books, 2017) and the creator of the JAWS (Jaffe WAR Score) metric for Hall of Fame analysis. He founded the Futility Infielder website (2001), was a columnist for Baseball Prospectus (2005-2012) and a contributing writer for Sports Illustrated (2012-2018). He has been a recurring guest on MLB Network and a member of the BBWAA since 2011, and a Hall of Fame voter since 2021. Follow him on BlueSky @jayjaffe.bsky.social.

item.title: [blogs.fangraphs.com] FanGraphs Power Rankings: September 14–20

item.content:encoded:
We’ve made it to the final week of the regular season. There are still two divisions in the American League up for grabs, a couple of long-shot playoff hopefuls looking to make a last-minute run, and playoff seeding to fight over. It should make for a dramatic end to a great season.
Our power rankings use a modified Elo rating system. If you’re familiar with chess rankings, you’ll know that Elo is an elegant ranking format that measures teams’ relative strength and is very reactive to recent performance. To avoid overweighting recent results during the season, we weigh each team’s raw Elo rank using our coin flip playoff odds (specifically, we regress the playoff odds by 50% and weigh those against the raw Elo ranking, increasing in weight as the season progresses to a maximum of 25%). The weighted Elo ranks are then displayed as “Power Score” in the tables below. As the best and worst teams sort themselves out between now and October, they’ll filter to the top and bottom of the rankings, while the exercise remains reactive to hot streaks and cold snaps. If you’re looking for a visual representation of the ups and downs of your team throughout the season, look no further than the brand new Power Rankings Board in the FanGraphs Lab.
First up are the full rankings, presented in a sortable table. Below that, I’ve grouped the teams into tiers with comments on a handful of clubs. You’ll notice that the official ordinal rankings don’t always match the tiers — there are times where I take editorial liberties when grouping teams together — but generally, the ordering is consistent. One thing to note: The playoff odds listed in the tables below are our standard Depth Charts odds, not the coin flip odds that are used in the ranking formula.
| Rank | Team | W-L | Hot/Cold | Elo | Opp Elo | Playoff% | Power Score | Δ |

| 7 | BOS | 84-72 | — | 1544 | 1500 | 100.0% | 1594 | -3 |

🛣️ Avg opp Elo >1525 (last 10) | ⛵ Avg opp Elo <1475 (last 10)
…
| Team | Record | Elo | Opponent Elo | Playoff Odds | Power Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Brewers | 98-58 | 1602 | 1496 | 100.0% | 1637 |
| Rays | 95-60 | 1594 | 1489 | 100.0% | 1631 |
It was a great week for the Brewers. They won their fourth straight NL Central title and sixth in the last nine years, and also set another franchise record for wins in a single season, one year after setting the previous record. They now have a chance to win 100 games for the first time in club history this week and still have the top seed in the NL to play for.
The Rays swept the Athletics and won their series against the Red Sox last week to put some distance between themselves and the Yankees in the AL East race. The gap in the division is now six games, and even though the two rivals play each other four times during the final week of the season, it would take a massive collapse from Tampa Bay to upset the current standings. Because the Rays also currently lead the season series with the Yankees, 6-3, all they need is to win one of the four games in New York to take the division title. With Shane McClanahan still recovering from his forearm injury — his availability for the playoffs is up in the air — Freddy Peralta has stepped up to lead the pitching staff over the last few weeks. Across his last five starts, he’s allowed just three runs in 28 2/3 innings. That’s the kind of production the Rays were hoping to get when they acquired him at the trade deadline.
| Team | Record | Elo | Opponent Elo | Playoff Odds | Power Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dodgers | 96-60 | 1580 | 1492 | 100.0% | 1621 |
| Padres | 87-69 | 1578 | 1501 | 97.2% | 1618 |
| Braves | 92-64 | 1565 | 1500 | 100.0% | 1610 |
| Yankees | 89-66 | 1556 | 1497 | 100.0% | 1603 |
The Dodgers are getting all their pieces in place for the postseason. Andy Pages and Roki Sasaki will be activated off the IL on Tuesday, and Shohei Ohtani should follow on Wednesday. There’s a lingering question about Blake Snell’s status after he injured his groin last week, but it sounds like he’ll be able to make a start during the final weekend of the season. And even though the majority of the year has been a slog for Kyle Tucker, his bat seems to have finally woken up at the right time; he collected nine hits and three home runs last week.
Having won 13 of their last 14 games, the Padres are peaking at exactly the right moment. They’ve surged five games ahead of the Diamondbacks and one ahead of the Phillies in the NL Wild Card standings, and are now tied with the Cubs for the top spot. San Diego’s final series of the season against Arizona still looms large, especially if the Friars stumble against the Dodgers in the series beforehand. You’re probably familiar with Fernando Tatis Jr.’s hot streak — he blasted four home runs last week to bring his total in September up to eight — but the biggest contributor to the Padres’ success recently has been Ty France. He had 12 hits and a home run last week and has posted a fantastic 168 wRC+ during the second half of the season.
After a couple of years away from the top, the Braves are NL East champions again — it’s their seventh division title in the last nine years. Atlanta’s dominance this year has been a welcome return to form. Even though his season has been a bit up and down, Ronald Acuña Jr. is looking like the superstar that won the MVP back in 2023 again. Last week, he smacked three home runs, including a go-ahead grand slam on Saturday, and is running a 191 wRC+ in September.
A little more than a week after being activated off the IL, Aaron Judge is back on the shelf, this time with a calf injury sustained on Wednesday. His availability for the playoffs is still up in the air, though he’s confident that he’ll be able to return sooner rather than later. Thankfully, Jazz Chisholm Jr. should be activated off the IL on Tuesday, and there’s some confidence that Trent Grisham will also be ready to return for the postseason. It helps that Ben Rice has bounced back from a rough August to post a 192 wRC+ in September. Still, Judge’s injury is a major blow to the Yankees’ hopes for a deep October run.
| Team | Record | Elo | Opponent Elo | Playoff Odds | Power Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Red Sox | 84-72 | 1544 | 1500 | 100.0% | 1594 |
| Phillies | 86-70 | 1546 | 1501 | 97.3% | 1593 |
| Cubs | 87-69 | 1539 | 1501 | 99.9% | 1590 |
Even though the Red Sox lost both of their series last week, they managed to clinch a postseason berth on Sunday. It’s the cap to a remarkable turnaround after the team looked completely lost in mid-June. Boston can officially secure the second Wild Card spot with a couple of wins against the Guardians this week. Then the team can turn its attention to the Yankees and the rematch of last year’s Wild Card matchup between these two historic rivals.
Nothing is going to come easy for the Phillies over the next few weeks. The team placed Jesús Luzardo on the IL last week with a shoulder injury, but thankfully, it sounds like he’ll be ready to pitch in the playoffs. But before they count their chickens, they need to actually clinch a playoff spot. Philadelphia is four games up on the Diamondbacks in the NL Wild Card race, but its upcoming opponents are no cake walk; the Phillies have the Brewers and Rays on the schedule to finish off the regular season. Facing two of the best teams in baseball is quite a test ahead of the postseason, and the Phillies haven’t exactly been playing well lately.
The biggest concern for the Cubs right now is the status of Alex Bregman. He was struck by a foul ball in the face while standing in the on-deck circle during Sunday’s game and was taken to the hospital for further evaluation. Alongside Pete Crow-Armstrong, Bregman has been one of the best hitters in baseball since the All-Star break. It would be a huge blow if the third baseman had to miss any significant amount of time at this point in the season. As for Crow-Armstrong, he’s two stolen bases away from joining the 40/40 club. He put a few finishing touches on his MVP case last week by bopping four more home runs, bringing his season total up to 45.
| Team | Record | Elo | Opponent Elo | Playoff Odds | Power Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guardians | 81-75 | 1520 | 1498 | 97.6% | 1572 |
| White Sox | 80-76 | 1494 | 1500 | 96.2% | 1552 |
| Rangers | 78-78 | 1502 | 1496 | 56.5% | 1517 |
| Astros | 77-79 | 1493 | 1493 | 45.8% | 1481 |
There was some upheaval in the two division races represented in this tier. Entering last week one game behind the White Sox in the AL Central standings, the Guardians took two of three games against the South Siders in a dramatic series, which included a walk-off on Tuesday and an improbable go-ahead homer on Wednesday. From there, although Chicago took advantage of playing — and winning — on Thursday while Cleveland was off to pull back into a tie atop the division, the Guardians just kept winning, sweeping the the Athletics over the weekend to bring their winning streak to five. José Ramírez finally broke out of his extended slump, tallying nine hits, a home run, and four stolen bases last week.
As for the White Sox, they won three of their four games against the the Tigers, but that one loss was enough to drop them to a game behind Cleveland in the Central. Still, the Sox have a three-game cushion for the final AL Wild Card spot, and they own the tiebreaker over the Guardians, meaning both first place and a potential first-round bye are still in their sights. Miguel Vargas is carrying most of the load for the lineup right now, hitting three home runs last week, but he needs some support if Chicago wants to make some noise in the postseason.
Over in the AL West, the Astros were swept by the Braves this past weekend, allowing the Rangers to jump into first place with a .500 record. Texas enters this week one game up, but crucially Houston holds the tiebreaker. If the Rangers can manage to hang on, it would be just their second postseason appearance in the last decade. The last time they made the playoffs, they won the World Series.
The Houston bullpen was responsible for the backbreaking losses on Saturday and Sunday, but the lack of offense has been a much bigger problem. Over the Astros’ last 10 games, they’ve scored more than four runs in a game just once. Yordan Alvarez looked fine last week (eight hits, including two home runs) after his ankle scare the previous weekend, and Jeremy Peña has been great too (10 hits, three homers), but the rest of the lineup has been struggling. During this 10-game stretch, Houston hitters not named Alvarez or Peña have combined for an ugly 55 wRC+.
| Team | Record | Elo | Opponent Elo | Playoff Odds | Power Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Diamondbacks | 82-74 | 1527 | 1505 | 5.6% | 1464 |
| Blue Jays | 77-79 | 1516 | 1504 | 3.6% | 1456 |
The Diamondbacks managed to keep their slim playoff hopes alive with a pair of wins over the Yankees on Saturday and Sunday. The first victory was a walk-off and the second was highlighted by a go-ahead grand slam from Nolan Arenado. Arizona needs to take care of business in Colorado and get some help from the Dodgers to ensure that the final series against the Padres has some stakes. There’s a chance the Phillies could crash out, opening another window for the Snakes, but the direct path is through San Diego.
The Blue Jays’ hopes for a last-minute surge into the playoffs were dashed last week when they lost both of their series to the Tigers and Rangers. They’re three games back and have the Astros to contend with if they want to try and sneak into that final Wild Card spot. It’s probably too little, too late, but the team is activating Trey Yesavage off the IL on Monday as one more reinforcement ahead of a final push.
| Team | Record | Elo | Opponent Elo | Playoff Odds | Power Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pirates | 79-77 | 1534 | 1509 | 0.0% | 1465 |
| Mets | 71-85 | 1508 | 1509 | 0.0% | 1446 |
| Orioles | 75-81 | 1493 | 1504 | 0.1% | 1435 |
| Marlins | 76-80 | 1476 | 1503 | 0.0% | 1422 |
| Tigers | 73-83 | 1470 | 1491 | 0.0% | 1417 |
| Reds | 72-84 | 1469 | 1508 | 0.0% | 1416 |
The series between the Orioles and Mets last week in Queens turned out to be more interesting than you’d expect from two teams mired in hugely disappointing seasons. Pete Alonso made his first appearance as a member of the opposing team at Citi Field and wound up hitting his 300th career home run on Tuesday, a game-tying shot in the ninth inning. He received a huge ovation from the hometown crowd, which drew some irksome comments from a few Mets players and staff after the game. Baltimore wound up sweeping New York to cut its deficit in the AL Wild Card race to 2.5 games. Alas, a sweep by the Brewers over the weekend slammed the door shut on any playoff hopes the O’s still had.
Even though the Marlins’ season essentially ended with that 12-game losing streak back in July, they have made some significant progress in their quest to become a contending club. Otto Lopez looks like a star they can build the lineup around, while Eury Pérez and Max Meyer should be strong enough to anchor the pitching staff in the years ahead. There’s also a cohort of young prospects in the upper minors who should be making their debuts soon. The future in Miami is brighter than it’s been in a while.
This is the huge step forward the Reds were hoping to see from Elly De La Cruz. In September, he has blasted seven home runs, including in five straight games earlier this month, and is running a major league-best 236 wRC+. It’s too bad the rest of Cincinnati’s roster is a bit of a mess. Sal Stewart has been excellent as De La Cruz’s sidekick, but the starting rotation has struggled mightily, and the big injury to Hunter Greene has thrown the ceiling of that group up in the air heading into next year. Still, building around a superstar like De La Cruz should make things easier if the resources to improve the rest of the roster are made available.

| Angels | 60-96 | 1409 | 1498 | 0.0% | 1371 |

| Rockies | 57-99 | 1373 | 1507 | 0.0% | 1344 |
The AL Central crown runs through Kansas City; both the White Sox and Guardians travel to face the Royals during the final week of the season. Unfortunately, the Royals haven’t been playing well enough recently to act as a spoiler. They ended August with a 13-3 stretch, but they’ve been the worst team in the AL in September, with just five wins in 18 games.
It took a lot longer than expected, but the Twins were finally eliminated from the playoff race last week. It was a drama-filled week, too. They won a wild extra-inning walk-off affair against the Yankees on Wednesday and then were walked-off twice against the Angels between two shutout victories over the weekend. Even though they all made their big league debuts over the last few weeks, Walker Jenkins, Kaelen Culpepper, and Emmanuel Rodriguez never all appeared in a game together. That trio represents the future of the organization, so it’s a little disappointing that that future couldn’t be realized in a small way this year.

item.title: [mlb.com] Postseason FAQ: What's next for the Red Sox?
item.dc:creator: Ian Browne

item.content:encoded:
Now, they have six regular-season games left to prepare for what is to come.
One big objective will be to get postseason baseball back to Fenway Park for the first time since 2021. After losing in three games in the 2025 AL Wild Card Series to the Yankees at Yankee Stadium, the ending felt too abrupt.
It has already been an improbable turnaround for the Red Sox, surging from 14 games under .500 on June 25 and getting to the postseason. There is a belief within the clubhouse that more magic can happen.
“I think we can make a run,” said rookie lefty Payton Tolle. “I think we’ve got the guys. I think we can get hot. We’re just going to continue to play the way that we play. That team baseball we’ve been playing. You play to get to the postseason and to give yourself a shot to go to the World Series.”
Without further ado, here are some key talking points heading into the playoffs.
What could the postseason roster look like?
C: Adley Rutschman, Connor Wong
1B: Willson Contreras
2B: Nick Sogard
SS: Trevor Story
3B: Caleb Durbin
UTIL: Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Mickey Gasper
OF: Jarren Duran, Ceddanne Rafaela, Wilyer Abreu, Braiden Ward
DH: Roman Anthony, Jahmai Jones
SP: Sonny Gray, Ranger Suarez, Payton Tolle
Bullpen: Aroldis Chapman, Garrett Whitlock, Tyron Guerrero, Erik Miller, Greg Weissert, Brayan Bello, Jake Bennett, Garrett Crochet, Tanner Houck
The most intriguing decision for the position-player roster surrounds whether to add Ward, who set the Triple-A Worcester record with 61 stolen bases this season, as a pinch-running specialist. Dave Roberts, anyone?
The bullpen situation also bears watching. Considering that Crochet hasn’t pitched since April 25 and Houck’s next appearance will be his first in the Majors since 2025, the club will monitor how both rehabbers are throwing before finalizing the roster. This could influence if the club carries Bennett as a reliever. Jovani Morán is another option from the left side.
When does the postseason begin?
For the Red Sox, the fun starts on Sept. 29, when interim manager Chad Tracy’s club participates in an AL Wild Card Series, with all games in the best-of-three series to be played on the road. The Yankees, unless they improbably take the AL East from the Rays, will be the Red Sox opponent in what will be yet another chapter in the richest rivalry in baseball. The only other scenario that can stave off another rivalry match would be the Red Sox slipping to the No. 6 seed. They lead the current No. 6 seed, the White Sox, by four games.
How have the Red Sox performed against the Yankees this season?
Last year, Boston’s hopes of getting a playoff game at Fenway Park for the first time since ‘21 ended when the team lost Game 3 of the Wild Card Series to … the Yankees in the Bronx. So, yes, this would be a rematch between the rivals. In a form befitting the rivalry, the regular-season series swayed back and forth, with New York ultimately taking seven of the 13 head-to-head encounters.
The Yankees swept the Red Sox at Fenway from April 21-23 in what wound up being Alex Cora’s last home series managing Boston. Fast forward to the Bronx from June 5-7, and the sides split, with the middle game getting postponed due to rain. For the Red Sox, their entire season started to turn around with a four-game sweep at Fenway from June 25-28. And for the Yankees, home field for this potential series was essentially wrapped up when they took three out of four from the Sox at the end of August to clinch the season series.
Will Aaron Judge be active for the Wild Card Series?
Judge’s potential participation in the series will be a huge focal point. The Yankees’ captain, limited to 66 games this season, was recently placed on the injured list again with a right calf strain. Though the Yankees have played more games without Judge than with him, his absence could make a difference for Boston.
What happens in the unlikely scenario the Red Sox slip from the No. 5 seed to the No. 6 spot?
In that case, the Red Sox would play the division champion with the worst record, which at this point would be whoever emerges victorious in a shaky AL West.
Which health situations should be monitored as the regular season winds down?
Where to start? There are many to choose from.
Contreras suffered a badly bruised knuckle between his right ring finger and pinkie when he was hit by a pitch on Sept. 17. He admitted he will be out for “days,” but hopes to be back before the postseason. It was a good sign that Contreras was able to grip a bat and take some swings on Sunday.
All eyes will be on Crochet to see if it’s possible to activate him for the playoffs as a reliever even though he hasn’t pitched since April 25 due to left shoulder inflammation.
Rafaela, the Red Sox's All-Star center fielder, has been out since Sept. 3 with a right quadriceps strain but should return before the regular season ends.
How does the rotation line up for the Red Sox?
If not for the near season-long loss of Crochet to this point, the Game 1 starter wouldn’t be in question. Tracy reordered his rotation for the upcoming series, going with Tolle on Tuesday against the Guardians, followed by Gray on Wednesday and Suarez on Thursday. Could this be the same order the Sox open the playoffs with? Tracy isn’t ready to reveal those plans yet.
How much postseason experience does Boston’s projected roster have?
Contreras and Chapman both won World Series rings while playing for the 2016 Cubs. Chapman added another one with the Rangers in ‘23. Kiner-Falefa was with Toronto last season, meaning he got to play in the epic Dodgers-Blue Jays World Series, losing one of the most dramatic Game 7s ever.
Rutschman played in five postseason games during his time with the Orioles, but none beyond the Division Series. Several players in Boston’s young core got their first taste of postseason experience last year in Abreu, Rafaela and Duran. Durbin went to the NLCS with the Brewers in ‘25. Houck and Whitlock are the only players remaining on the Boston team that came two wins from making the World Series in ‘21. Veteran shortstop Story had a solid Wild Card Series in the Bronx last year.
Suarez (4-1, 1.48 ERA in 11 outings, eight starts) had his share of October moments in Philadelphia, and Gray has a 3.26 ERA in six career playoff starts.

item.title: [mlb.com] Who sits atop final Power Rankings of the regular season?
item.dc:creator: Will Leitch
item.description: These are the last MLB.com Power Rankings of the 2026 regular season. In exactly one week, 18 of these teams will go home, and 12 will be left. We have made it all the way through. Since these will be the final rankings, let’s take a look at each team, even the ones who did not make the playoffs, and find something positive its fanbase can feel about the 2026 season … now that it’s almost in the rearview mirror. These rankings, as always, are compiled from MLB.com contributors whose names you ca
item.content:encoded:
These are the last MLB.com Power Rankings of the 2026 regular season. In exactly one week, 18 of these teams will go home, and 12 will be left. We have made it all the way through. Since these will be the final rankings, let’s take a look at each team, even the ones who did not make the playoffs, and find something positive its fanbase can feel about the 2026 season … now that it’s almost in the rearview mirror.
These rankings, as always, are compiled from MLB.com contributors whose names you can find at the bottom of this (and every) piece, but the words are mine. If you dislike the rankings, yell at all of us. But if you dislike the words, feel free to yell at me.
Also, as we close the season, we note for each team the highest they were ranked in our Power Rankings all season -- when they hit the peak.
1. Brewers (previously: 1)
Season High Water Mark: 1, this week
It’s the best season in Brewers history. It sure looks like they’re going to win 100 games for the first time ever. They’ve got a Cy Young frontrunner in Jacob Misiorowski, they’ve got all the momentum, and they’ve got a team that wins by doing all the little things right. Last year was a huge postseason bummer. Now is the time to right that wrong.
2. Dodgers (previously: 2)
Season High Water Mark: 1, Aug. 17
The Dodgers have had a lot of drama this year, much of it revolving around a hugely disappointing first season at Chavez Ravine for Kyle Tucker and injury concerns for Shohei Ohtani. And yet here they are, one of the best teams in baseball, as always, and the team everyone knows is looming in October.
3. Rays (previously: 4)
Season High Water Mark: 2, May 25
Don’t forget, almost no one picked the Rays to win the tough AL East this year. But it looks like it’s going to be theirs, with a deep, versatile roster led by Junior Caminero, who looks like he’s going to be a signature star in this league for the next decade-plus.
4. Braves (previously: 3)
Season High Water Mark: 1, June 15
Every year since their World Series title in 2021 has felt a little bit like a disappointment in its own way, even the 104-win season in '23. But this one sure hasn’t, with the Braves overcoming a '25 losing season by winning the division again. And check out Ronald Acuña Jr., who looks like a superstar again.
5. Yankees (previously: 5)
Season High Water Mark: 2, May 4
For a long time, it was assumed that if Aaron Judge was hurt for an extended period of time, the Yankees were cooked. But thanks to a fantastic pitching staff -- including Cy Young frontrunner Cam Schlittler -- the Yankees look as strong as ever. But it still may all ride on Judge regardless.
6. Cubs (previously: 6)
Season High Water Mark: 1, May 11
What more can you say about Pete Crow-Armstrong at this point? He’s about to end the Shohei Ohtani MVP reign, and he’s doing so while becoming one of the most popular players in the sport and having one of the best seasons in Cubs history. And it sure feels like October is going to fit him like a glove.
7. Red Sox (previously: 8)
Season High Water Mark: 6, Aug. 5
This season looked absolutely lost in June, and Red Sox fans were tearing their hair out. Then, suddenly, the Sox were playing the best of any team in baseball, and they rode that run all the way to a playoff spot. And it's sure looking like we'll get another installment of The Rivalry in the Wild Card.
8. Padres (previously: 9)
Season High Water Mark: 3, April 20
The Padres have justified all the investments A.J. Preller and company have made in the offseason with this late-season run, but they still have won just one game past the Division Series round this century. The top of the NL is tough this year, but no one’s hotter than the Padres.
9. Phillies (previously: 7)
Season High Water Mark: 5, July 16
It has been a rocky road, with Don Mattingly taking over early in the season, the team righting itself, and then struggling down the stretch. But in this ear, all that matters for the Phillies is the postseason. All of their questions are about to be answered, one way or the other.
10. Guardians (previously: 12)
Season High Water Mark: 5, June 8
The Guardians’ fight back to the top of the AL Central wasn’t as dramatic as last year’s, but if they can end up atop the division when it’s all said and done, it won’t matter. And if they do … they might just get a first-round bye out of it.
11. White Sox (previously: 11)
Season High Water Mark: 6, June 15
If the White Sox aren’t able to get into the playoffs after the fun season they’ve had, it will feel like a heartbreaker, but it probably shouldn’t be. This is a team that has lost 100-plus games for three consecutive seasons! Look at where they are now! The playoffs would be wonderful. But what a major step forward they’ve made. With more to come.
12. Rangers (previously: 16)
Season High Water Mark: 8, April 3
The Rangers have never gotten higher than three games over .500 this year … but that has not kept them out of the middle of the AL West, and even atop the division. They’ve only made the playoffs once in the last decade -- the year they won the World Series. That may well change this season.
13. Diamondbacks (previously: 10)
Season High Water Mark: 9, Aug. 17
The Padres’ torrid run down the stretch may end up keeping Arizona out of the playoffs, though the season’s final series between the two teams could have something to say about that. But a year of uncertainty ended up being a positive one, despite some off-field drama … and there’s still time left in this one.
14. Astros (previously: 13)
Season High Water Mark: 7, April 6
Yordan Alvarez had a fully healthy season and responded with an all-timer of an offensive performance. The only question now is whether they can catch the intrastate-rival Rangers for the AL West crown -- and it looks like they're going to have to, if they want to make the playoffs at all.
15. Blue Jays (previously: 14)
Season High Water Mark: 2, March 23
It looked for a while like the Jays, after the brutal way they lost the World Series last year, would make up for a disappointing season by sneaking into the final Wild Card spot. How fans feel about this season may depend on whether or not they can crawl their way back in. It’s going to be an uphill climb.
16. Pirates (previously: 15)
Season High Water Mark: 5, April 20
Pirates fans had big hopes for this year, and while they weren’t the playoff team that some had expected, they nevertheless have won 79 games and could notch their first winning season since 2018. It’s progress.
17. Orioles (previously: 19)
Season High Water Mark: 10, March 23
It may have hurt to do it, but the O’s did maximize their return for Adley Rutschman with even more young players to add to the ones they already have. It’s understandable if O’s fans are skeptical, but you can’t argue that Pete Alonso was a great investment, and really a North Star for the whole franchise at this point.
18. Marlins (previously: 18)
Season High Water Mark: 8, July 16
Take away that 12-game losing streak, and the Marlins are a playoff team this year. You obviously can’t do that, but the different way the Marlins have been doing things started to pay off this year. And they may well have a star in Otto Lopez.
19. Tigers (previously: 21)
Season High Water Mark: 8, April 27
This turned out to be their first losing season since 2023, which is frustrating because hopes were so high heading into the year, but there is still a ton of young talent here, led by Riley Greene, who is quietly putting together a stellar start to his career. And with the Tarik Skubal trade, there’s even more young talent on the way.
20. Cardinals (previously: 17)
Season High Water Mark: 8, May 18
The bullpen fell apart down the stretch, making the record look worse than the season felt, but the Cardinals made many steps forward this year, particularly with the lineup: Jordan Walker, JJ Wetherholt, Joshua Báez, Alec Burleson and Leo Bernal all look like lineup mainstays … with even more talent coming down the pipe.
21. Nationals (previously: 24)
Season High Water Mark: 12, June 22
James Wood is a star, but he was hardly the only National to emerge in 2026, with CJ Abrams and the recently extended Cade Cavalli setting themselves up as players the Nationals can build around. The offense was terrific this year: That’s the first time you’ve been able to say that in a long time.
22. Mariners (previously: 20)
Season High Water Mark: 3, March 23
So, yeah, it was a bit of a disaster season for the Mariners, in just about every possible way. But this was not a now-or-never season for the M’s: They have a very exciting rotation for 2027, and note that Cal Raleigh started to warm up as the season came to a close as well.
23. Mets (previously: 23)
Season High Water Mark: 5, March 23
That most of the offseason moves blew up in their faces is the reason they’re not in the playoffs, but they certainly played well enough in the second half to look like a playoff team, thanks largely to rookies Carson Benge, A.J. Ewing and Nolan McLean. The Mets will look different next year, but that’s a good thing.
24. Twins (previously: 22)
Season High Water Mark: 15, Aug. 5
The next generation of Twins stars has arrived: Kaelen Culpepper, Walker Jenkins and Emmanuel Rodriguez all made their debut this year (and still have Rookie of the Year eligibility for next season). This was a transition year for the Twins. There’s plenty of reason to think they can turn the corner in 2027.
25. Reds (previously: 25)
Season High Water Mark: 6, April 27
This was the superstar step forward the Reds have been waiting for from Elly De La Cruz. They no longer have to wonder if he’s ever going to make the leap: He now has. And remember, he is still only 24 years old.
26. Royals (previously: 26)
Season High Water Mark: 14, May 11
Not much went the way it was supposed to this year, but there’s still a lot of young talent here. And there is Bobby Witt Jr., who, even in a down power year (for him), leads the American League in WAR, per FanGraphs.
27. Giants (previously: 27)
Season High Water Mark: 18, March 23
The terrible start, and the occasional discord and chaos, made this season feel like it was over with before it even began. But don’t overlook the fact that Rafael Devers, for most of this season, looked like the superstar the Giants traded for.
28. Angels (previously: 29)
Season High Water Mark: 19, April 20
A potential sale of the team is something that fans have wondered could change the trajectory of this franchise, and they’re going to get the opportunity to find out. There’s some young talent starting to percolate here, perhaps most notably Walbert Ureña, a 22-year-old who looks like he might already be an ace.
29. A’s (previously: 28)
Season High Water Mark: 10, May 11
The onslaught of injuries to their position players made people forget how good this lineup was at some point, and how late in the year they were in contention. As they move closer to their move to Las Vegas, there’s still plenty to build on here … and plenty of reason to have optimism for the future.
30. Rockies (previously: 30)
Season High Water Mark: 27, May 4
It does not look like the Rockies are going to avoid 100 losses this year, alas, marking four straight years with 100-plus losses. But they’ll still be double-digit games better than they were last year, and they’ll do so with a front office that seems, at last, to have a clear plan moving forward.
Voters: Jason Catania, Dan Cichalski, Theo DeRosa, Rick Gold Jr., Jared Greenspan, Will Leitch, Brent Maguire, Travis Miller, Brian Murphy, Arturo Pardavila, Shanthi Sepe-Chepuru, Andrew Simon, David Venn, Andy Werle.
